# Blast contracts: integrator reference

> Everything an integrator needs to understand and call Blast's Sui Move contracts: a bonding-curve launchpad whose graduated coins migrate into Cetus or Bluefin pools, standalone overflow presales, partner fee codes, Boost leverage coins on Aftermath perpetuals, and the funSUI/blastSUI staking vault. Sui mainnet only.

This file is self-contained. Give it to an AI agent and ask it anything about Blast's contracts. An agent that needs one product can take that product's smaller file instead: [Presale](https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/llms/presale.txt), [Launchpad](https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/llms/launchpad.txt), [Partner codes](https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/llms/partners.txt), [Boosts](https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/llms/boosts.txt), [blastSUI and funSUI](https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/llms/blast-sui.txt), [Shared core](https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/llms/core.txt), [LP vault](https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/llms/vault.txt), [Administration](https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/llms/admin.txt).

How it is organized:

1. **Packages and deployment status**: each package, whether it is live on Sui mainnet, and its IDs.
2. **Guides**: how each product works end to end, starting with the calling conventions every product shares. Each product guide opens with its deployment status. Use them for behavior, flows, economics, and pitfalls.
3. **API reference**: generated from the Move source. Every public function and type with its doc comment, every event, every abort code, and the package constants. Use it for exact signatures and field layouts.

When the guides and the reference disagree, the reference is right: it is generated from the source on every change. When this file does not say a behavior exists, treat it as unsupported. Source for every module is linked from the reference ([repository](https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts)).

Conventions: amounts are atomic units of the coin named; rates are basis points (BPS) out of 10,000; timestamps are Unix milliseconds from Sui's shared `Clock` at `0x6`, while durations and delays are elapsed milliseconds. Types are written as Move: `module::Type` names a type in another module of the same package, `package::module::Type` one in another Blast package, and well-known Sui framework types appear bare.

## Packages and deployment status

Call a live package at its package ID (`published-at`). Types and events are named by the package that first defined them (`original-id`), which stays the same across upgrades.

| Package | Product | Status | Package ID (`published-at`) | Type origin (`original-id`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `blast_fun_migrators` | Migration and LP vaults | not yet published | — | — |
| `blast_partners` | Partner codes | not yet published | — | — |
| `blast_boosts_core` | Boosts core | live; source has changed since | `0xac10e88ff25bd98a841f60cfcdc4006b4ad3d3afb577b5024043798ff7f4cafe` | `0xac10e88ff25bd98a841f60cfcdc4006b4ad3d3afb577b5024043798ff7f4cafe` |
| `blast_boosts_products` | Boost product tags | live; source has changed since | `0xe9b3d42d4e4f6a97aaa43884b155c42abd8c2c62bba9a51e8847d7b05f3717ba` | `0xe9b3d42d4e4f6a97aaa43884b155c42abd8c2c62bba9a51e8847d7b05f3717ba` |

## Calling Blast contracts

Every Blast product is a set of Sui Move packages called from programmable
transaction blocks (PTBs). This section covers what every product shares. Each
product guide below assumes it.

### Products and packages

| Product | What users do | Packages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Presale | commit Quote to a capped or overflow sale, claim tokens or refunds, earn LP fees and holder rewards after migration | `blast_presale`; one-off partner migrators such as `blast_aftermath_dao_presale` |
| Launchpad | launch a coin on a bonding curve, trade it, graduate it into a DEX pool | `blast_fun` (curve, lifecycle, fees), a generated coin package per launch, `blast_fun_migrators` (venue start, migration, LP vault, LP fees, holder rewards) |
| Partner codes | earn a share of Blast's fee on the flow an app brings | `blast_partners` |
| Boosts | hold a leveraged long or short coin backed by Aftermath perpetuals | `blast_boosts_core`, `blast_boosts_products`, `blast_boosts_aftermath` |
| blastSUI | stake SUI with one validator through funSUI and blastSUI | `blast_sui` |
| Administration | Blast's operators manage roles, fees, and upgrades | `blast_admin` |

Each package and what it depends on:

```text
blast_fun_migrators          -> blast_fun, blast_admin, Cetus, Bluefin
blast_fun                    -> blast_partners, blast_admin
blast_partners               -> blast_admin
blast_presale                -> blast_admin, blast_partners, blast_fun_vesting, Cetus, Bluefin, Aftermath
blast_aftermath_dao_presale  -> blast_presale, Aftermath AMM
blast_boosts_aftermath       -> blast_boosts_core, blast_partners, blast_admin, Aftermath perpetuals
blast_boosts_core            -> blast_admin
blast_sui                    -> blast_admin, Sui system
blast_admin                  -> Sui framework only
```

The launchpad imports no DEX. A migrator package depends on the launchpad and
composes with it inside one PTB. Presale uses typed roles from the shared
`blast_admin` ACL and holds migrated liquidity in its own `presale_vault::Vault`.
Use the presale guide for presale calls.

`blast_fun_vesting` (used by `blast_presale`) lives in this repository at
`sui/vesting` and is immutable on mainnet. The standalone
OTC package lives at `sui/otc`. See the [utility integration guide](https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/docs/utilities.md).

### Time values

Timestamp parameters ending in `_at_ms` are points in time measured in Unix
milliseconds. Duration parameters ending in `_duration_ms` are lengths of time;
`_delay_ms` parameters are offsets from the documented anchor. For example,
`commitment_starts_at_ms + commitment_duration_ms` is the commitment window's
end timestamp. Stored fields and event payloads retain their published names;
read their documented meaning rather than assuming every `_ms` value is a
timestamp. Framework calls such as `Clock::timestamp_ms` retain their native
names.

### Building a call

- **Target.** A call is `moveCall` with target
  `<package-id>::<module>::<function>`. Use the package ID (`published-at`) from
  the deployment table.
- **Type arguments.** Pass fully qualified type strings. A Blast type is named by
  the package that first defined it (`original-id`), even after an upgrade.
- **`TxContext`.** A trailing `ctx: &TxContext` or `&mut TxContext` parameter is
  supplied by Sui. Leave it out of the arguments.
- **Shared objects.** Pass a shared object by ID. A `&` parameter takes it
  read-only, `&mut` or by value takes it mutably; mutable access orders the
  transaction through consensus with every other writer of that object.
- **System objects.** `Clock` is `0x6` (always `&Clock`), the Sui system state is
  `0x5`, and the Coin Registry is `0xc`.
- **Coins in.** A function that takes `Coin<T>` by value consumes it whole. Split
  the exact amount first (`SplitCoins`; for SUI, split from the gas coin) and
  merge several coins first when needed (`MergeCoins`).
- **Values out.** Most Blast functions return coins and objects instead of
  transferring them. Every returned value without the `drop` ability must be used
  before the PTB ends: transfer it (`TransferObjects`), pass it to a later call,
  or merge it. A value with no abilities at all (a "hot potato", such as a
  launch initializer or a migration handoff) can only be consumed by the specific
  later call that accepts it, so the whole sequence must sit in one PTB.
- **Basis points.** Each package that takes rates defines its own validated
  `Bps` type in its `bps` module. Build one inside the PTB with that package's
  constructor, for example `blast_presale::bps::new` or `blast_fun::bps::new`,
  which aborts above 10,000. A `blast_fun` `Bps` is a different type from a
  `blast_presale` `Bps`.
- **Options.** Pass `Option<T>` arguments with `0x1::option::some` or
  `0x1::option::none` calls, or as pure BCS-encoded options.

### Reading state

- **Getters** are public functions that take `&` objects and return values. Run
  them through a dev-inspect or simulated transaction to read without signing
  or paying.
- **Object fields** can be read directly from a full node and decoded with BCS.
  The API reference prints every struct with its fields in declaration order,
  which is the BCS order. Fields are readable on chain even though Move code
  outside the module cannot access them.
- **Per-user records** (commitments, claims) usually live in dynamic fields
  keyed by a small key struct the reference lists; read them with the
  dynamic-field RPC calls.
- **Events** reconstruct history; contract state and completed events are the
  source of truth, and any off-chain preview is an estimate.

### Versions and upgrades

Upgrade rules depend on the package lineage.

| Posture | Packages | What callers do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Immutable | `blast_admin`, `blast_partners`, `blast_boosts_core`, `blast_aftermath_dao_presale` | Nothing: the code never changes. |
| Dependency-only | Historical presale publications | These older lineages can relink venue packages and do not use an operational version object. |
| Version-gated | `blast_presale`, `blast_fun`, `blast_fun_migrators`, `blast_sui`, `blast_boosts_aftermath` | Mutating calls take the package's shared version object. After an upgrade advances it, calls through an older package ID abort with a version mismatch, so always call the current ID. |
| Additive | `blast_boosts_products` | Upgrades only add product tags; it holds no state. |

### Events

- Query events by their Move type, named with the `original-id`.
- `blast_fun`, `blast_sui`, and `blast_boosts_aftermath` wrap every payload in
  the `Event<T>` envelope of their own `blast_events` module (for example
  `blast_fun::blast_events::Event`), so the event type is
  `<original-id>::blast_events::Event<<original-id>::<module>::<Payload>>`.
  Every other package emits payload structs directly.
- Sui orders events by checkpoint, transaction, and event index within the
  transaction; payloads carry no sequence numbers of their own.
- The reference lists every event struct under its module with its fields.

### Errors

A failed call returns a Move abort naming the module and function that aborted
and a `u64` code. Blast uses two styles:

- **Named errors** (`#[error]` constants): `blast_partners`,
  `blast_fun_migrators`, and `blast_aftermath_dao_presale`. Sui's RPC and SDKs
  decode these into the constant's name and message; the reference lists each
  module's constants with their messages.
- **Numeric codes**: `blast_fun`, `blast_presale`, `blast_sui`, `blast_boosts_core`,
  `blast_boosts_aftermath`, and `blast_admin` abort with small integers. Look the
  number up in that package's abort-code table in the reference.

The abort names the module where it happened, which may be a package called
underneath the one you called: a migrator call can abort inside `blast_fun` or
`blast_admin`, and an abort in a Cetus, Bluefin, or Aftermath module comes from
the venue. Simulate a transaction before signing to see its abort without
spending gas.

### Network

Blast deploys only to Sui mainnet. There is no testnet deployment, faucet, or
test address. Try a transaction with a mainnet simulation (dev-inspect or dry
run) before signing it.

## Presale

> **Deployment status:** `blast_presale` is not yet published on mainnet; its interface may change before publication. `blast_aftermath_dao_presale` is live on mainnet, published from an earlier revision; the source described here has changed since, so confirm signatures against the live package.

### What it is

`blast_presale` runs standalone presales on Sui mainnet. A creator brings a new coin
with zero supply. The sale mints the whole supply once, splits it between buyers, the launch
pool, Blast, and named recipients, and gives up mint authority forever. Buyers commit a Quote coin
(for example SUI) during a commitment window. By default commitments may exceed the raise target:
everyone is then filled at one common rate and the excess is refunded. A creator may instead
hard-cap the sale, from the start or from a later point in the window, so it takes Quote first
come, first served only up to the raise; such a sale may also close as soon as its raise is full. Anyone can migrate a funded sale into a
new full-range Cetus or Bluefin pool, or a 50/50 Aftermath pool behind Aftermath's DAO-fee pool;
the same transaction pays Blast (or, on a sale that names a partner, holds Blast's fees for a
later pay call), the raise recipients, and the token recipients. Buyers then claim their tokens
and overflow refund. A sale that misses its raise, or that someone cancels once its liquidity
deadline passes unmigrated, refunds every commitment in full. After migration a
`presale_vault::Vault` holds the LP position (for Cetus, its LP-burn proof; for Aftermath, the
DAO-fee pool's owner cap, the LP coin itself being sent to `0x0`) and splits its trading fees
between Blast, the creator's fee recipients, and holder-reward rounds.

The presale is separate from the bonding-curve launchpad and reuses the shared Blast
ACL, partner registry, and operational-version/capability-custody primitives.
Publication creates an owned `blast_presale_package::Publication`; it shares no
PackageVersion. `blast_presale::package_admin::wrap` consumes Publication and the
fresh matching UpgradeCap, sealing compatible custody and sharing the version
fully paused; publication-owned policy operations start with zero notice. Ordinary ACL-authorized operations
then configure policies before release.

See ADR 0117. In this guide `SaleToken` is the sale coin; venues call it `Meme`.

Routine state-changing public calls below take `&blast_presale_package::PackageVersion`
immediately after their first object argument, including initializer setters,
finalize/share, policy administration, migrations, payouts, and holder rewards.
It is a read-only shared input except during pause, unpause and upgrade commit-and-advance. A stale
or future generation aborts in `blast_admin::operational_version` before effects.
Pure value constructors, getters and `destroy_cap` do not take it. Initial policy
configuration uses the same version-guarded ACL operations as later changes.

### Objects and authority

Shared singletons, created once at deployment (`PackageAdmin` and `PackageVersion` by
`blast_presale::package_admin::wrap`, the others when the package is published):

- `fee_policy::FeePolicy`: Blast's current rates (`raise_bps`, `token_bps`, `lp_fee_meme_bps`,
  `lp_fee_quote_bps`, held in a `fee_policy::ProtocolFees`) that new sales snapshot, and the
  `destination` address every Blast payout goes to.
- `creation_policy::CreationPolicy`: the allowlists checked once, when a sale, or a vault without
  a presale, is created: Quote types, migrator witnesses, and Blast partners a sale may name.
- `blast_presale::venue_config::VenueConfig`: holds each Cetus sale's reserved pool-creation
  capability. Migration only borrows it; nothing removes it.
- `blast_presale::aftermath::PoolCreation<Lp, Meme, Quote>`: one per Aftermath sale, returned
  by `blast_presale::aftermath::finalize` and shared by `blast_presale::aftermath::share` in the
  same PTB; holds the Aftermath `CreatePoolCapV2` of the sale's fresh LP coin `Lp` and the sale's
  ID, so only that sale's migration can consume it.
- `blast_presale::aftermath::FinalizeTicket<Meme, Quote>`: a hot potato with no abilities that
  `blast_presale::aftermath::new` returns beside the `PresaleInitializer`; only
  `blast_presale::aftermath::finalize` consumes it, so the PTB that starts an Aftermath sale must
  finalize it there, or it fails with the ticket unconsumed.
- `blast_presale::package_admin::PackageAdmin`: holds the package's Publisher and compatible upgrade cap.
- `blast_presale::blast_presale_package::PackageVersion`: the singleton active generation and pause flags, shared by custody wrap.

Per-sale objects:

- `blast_presale::blast_presale::Presale<SaleToken, Quote>`: shared. It holds every commitment, the whole minted
  supply, and the sale's terms until migration or refund. It has `key` only, so it cannot be
  transferred: it must be shared in the transaction that creates it.
- `blast_presale::blast_presale::PresaleCap`: owned by the creator (key, store). It claims the vault's migration
  residuals and can be destroyed after a cancellation. It cannot change any sale term or move
  any commitment.
- `presale_vault::Vault<Meme, Quote>`: shared, created by a Cetus, Bluefin, or Aftermath
  migration or directly from its owner's position (see "Locking your own position without a
  presale"). It holds the LP position (Bluefin), the Cetus LP-burn proof (Cetus), or the DAO-fee
  pool's `OwnerCap` (Aftermath, whose LP coin is owned by `0x0`), the migration residuals, the
  holder-reward share of collected fees, and Blast's held LP fees on partnered sales. An
  Aftermath vault is also the address its DAO-fee pool pays fees to.
- `blast_presale::holder_rewards::Round<Meme, Quote>`: shared, one per published holder-reward round.
- A vesting schedule (`Vesting<T>` from the external, immutable `blast_fun_vesting` package):
  shared, one per vested payout. See "Claiming vested tokens".

Capabilities and who holds them:

| Object | Held by | Authorizes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blast_presale_package::Publication` | Deployer, until wrap consumes it permanently | Holds publication provenance until native custody is sealed; no policy authority. |
| `blast_acl::AdminCap` granted a presale role | Blast operations | The calls of each role it holds; see the table below. |
| `blast_presale::blast_presale::PresaleCap` | Sale creator (or a vendor treasury) | `presale_vault::claim_migration_residuals`, `blast_presale::blast_presale::destroy_cap`. |
| `blast_partners::blast_partners::Partner` | Shared, managed in `blast_partners` | Read by the presale to pay a partner its cut of Blast's fees. |

Blast administers presales through the one shared Blast access-control list
(`blast_admin::blast_acl`), as it does its other packages. `blast_presale_domain` declares the presale's roles; an operator's
`blast_acl::AdminCap` granted a role calls `blast_acl::sign_in<Role>` with the shared
`blast_acl::ACL` in the same PTB and passes the returned `blast_acl::AdminWitness<Role>` by
reference. Each admin call names exactly one role in its signature:

| Role | Calls |
| --- | --- |
| `blast_presale_domain::PauseAdmin` | `blast_presale_package::pause` |
| `blast_presale_domain::UnpauseAdmin` | `blast_presale::package_admin::unpause` |
| `blast_presale_domain::CancelAdmin` | Each `cancel_*` administrative operation |
| `blast_presale_domain::FeeAdmin` | `fee_policy::schedule_fees`, `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_protocol_fees`, `presale_vault::schedule_protocol_lp_fees`, `creation_policy::add_partner`, `creation_policy::remove_partner` |
| `blast_presale_domain::TreasuryAdmin` | `fee_policy::schedule_destination` |
| `blast_presale_domain::ListingAdmin` | `creation_policy::set_quote_allowed` |
| `blast_presale_domain::AdapterAdmin` | `creation_policy::schedule_migration_witness` |
| `blast_presale_domain::RewardsAdmin` | `blast_presale::holder_rewards::schedule_round`, `blast_presale::holder_rewards::schedule_round_delay`, `blast_presale::holder_rewards::settle_gas_reserve` |
| `blast_presale_domain::UpgradeAdmin` | `blast_presale::package_admin::authorize_upgrade`, `blast_presale::package_admin::commit_upgrade_and_advance` |

A role from another package, such as `blast_fun_domain::FeeAdmin`, is a different type and
cannot reach these calls. PauseAdmin may freeze creation, commitments or migration. No admin may cancel a sale, move commitments, change windows, recipients, or the fee split. Its
power over a live sale is limited to: its Blast rates before the window starts, its vault's Blast
LP-fee rates (from 0 to 3,000 BPS), the fee destination, and how the vault's
holder-reward share is distributed. A holder-reward round waits its vault's round notice after
`RewardsAdmin` schedules it; the notice starts at two hours, so `CancelAdmin` can stop a bad
round before anyone publishes it.

### Lifecycle

`blast_presale::blast_presale::Lifecycle` is one-way:

```
Pending --share--> Open --settle (total >= raise)--> Funded --migrate--> Migrated
                     \--settle (total < raise)--> Cancelled
                                 Funded --cancel_unlaunched (at LP deadline)--> Cancelled
```

| State | Exists | Allows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Pending` | Only inside the creation PTB, between `finalize` and `share` | `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_protocol_fees` (admin, when the creation PTB also signs in as `FeeAdmin`), `blast_presale::blast_presale::share` |
| `Open` | From `share` until `settle` | Before `start_ms`: `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_protocol_fees` (admin), which may only keep or lower each rate. From `start_ms` until `end_ms`: commits. From `end_ms`, or earlier once the raise is full under a hard cap that closes the sale when filled: `blast_presale::blast_presale::settle` |
| `Funded` | After a settle that met the raise | Migration at any time; `blast_presale::blast_presale::cancel_unlaunched` from the LP deadline |
| `Migrated` | After migration | `blast_presale::blast_presale::claim` (tokens + overflow refund), `blast_presale::blast_presale::pay_protocol_fees_with_partner` once on a partnered sale |
| `Cancelled` | After an underfunded settle or `cancel_unlaunched` | `blast_presale::blast_presale::claim` (full refund), `blast_presale::blast_presale::destroy_cap` |

Migration and cancellation race once the LP deadline passes: whichever transaction lands first
wins. Nobody can withdraw a commitment while the sale is `Open` or `Funded`.

### Flows

#### Publication and initial configuration

1. Publish the package. The deployer receives the unique `blast_presale::blast_presale_package::Publication`,
   holding its canonical Publisher and initial generation. Policy singletons are
   shared; no operational PackageVersion exists yet.
2. Call `blast_presale::package_admin::wrap` with Publication by value and the matching
   never-upgraded UpgradeCap. It consumes Publication permanently, seals native
   custody and shares PackageVersion. Publication-owned policy operations start with zero notice. All operations start paused (combined mask = 7).
3. Grant the required roles on the real Blast ACL. Configure destinations, fees
   and reviewed adapter admission through the ordinary schedule/apply operations
   with Clock. At zero delay these can run in one PTB. Quote admission uses its
   ordinary ListingAdmin setter. No publication proof authorizes policy changes.
4. Apply or cancel every outstanding zero-delay proposal. Use each operation's own
   role to schedule and apply its intended value and next notice. Upgrade custody
   already holds its 48-hour notice from publication.
   Read back every operation's notice and configured value before release.
5. Sign in as UnpauseAdmin and clear the intended bits on PackageVersion (all = 7) with
   `blast_presale::package_admin::unpause`. Unpause is immediate once every notice is guarded:
   the fee destination, the fee rates and the adapter set each need a nonzero applied notice, no
   pending proposal that would set it to zero, and no pending adapter admission. Otherwise it
   aborts with `blast_presale::errors::EUnguardedNotice` (6).

Setup may span transactions. Pausing and upgrades never reset the administrative
policy or recreate Publication. An outstanding zero-delay proposal remains ready
after enabling positive notices, which is why setup must settle those proposals
before release. Route admission remains checked when creating launches or sales.

PTB conventions used below: `Clock` is the shared object `0x6`. Values such as `Bps`,
`RecipientShare`, and `EligibilityPolicy` are structs, so build them with Move calls and pass the
results; plain numbers, booleans, addresses, and `vector<u8>` go in as pure inputs. Build a
`vector<RecipientShare>` with the PTB `MakeMoveVec` command (it may be empty).

#### Creating a sale

A sale is created in one PTB in three stages, the same shape as the launchpad's
`LaunchInitializer`: a venue migrator's `new` starts it and returns a
`blast_presale::blast_presale::PresaleInitializer<Meme, Quote>`; setters on the initializer record
the creator's terms; `blast_presale::blast_presale::finalize` checks them all together, mints the
supply, and returns the pending `Presale`, which `share` publishes. The initializer has no
abilities: `finalize` is the only way to consume it, so the PTB must finalize it.

Creators call a venue migrator's `new`, never `blast_presale::blast_presale::new` directly: that call needs the
migrator's witness, which only the migrator's module can construct. The venue is fixed for good
at creation. Who may call: *anyone* who owns a zero-supply `TreasuryCap<SaleToken>` and the
matching shared Coin Registry `Currency<SaleToken>`, for a Quote type and migrator the
`CreationPolicy` allows. The sale currency must have confirmed `Unregulated` status;
regulated coins and legacy currencies with `Unknown` status are rejected, including legacy
coins whose deny cap has not been registered. Create the sale coin through Coin Registry
without enabling regulation. Every setter and `finalize` take the initializer value from that PTB, so
only its creator can call them.

Value constructors (*anyone*, pure):

- `blast_presale::bps::new(value)` builds each rate; it aborts with
  `blast_presale::errors::EInvalidBps` above 10,000.
- `blast_presale::blast_presale::vesting_terms(vesting_cliff_delay_ms, vesting_period_duration_ms, periods)` returns a
  `blast_presale::blast_presale::VestingTerms`.
- `blast_presale::blast_presale::recipient_share(recipient, bps)` or
  `blast_presale::blast_presale::vested_recipient_share(recipient, bps, terms)` build one share. Gather them with
  `MakeMoveVec` into three lists: token recipients, raise recipients, and LP-fee recipients.
- `blast_presale::blast_presale::open_eligibility(wallet_cap, max_participants, min_commitment)` or
  `blast_presale::blast_presale::allowlisted_eligibility(root, leaf_count)` build the eligibility policy.
- `blast_presale::blast_presale::uncapped_for_eligible(starts_after_ms)` or
  `blast_presale::blast_presale::uncapped_for_anyone(starts_after_ms, max_participants, min_commitment)` build an
  uncapped phase.
- `blast_presale::blast_presale::fee_split(fee_recipients, holder_rewards_bps)` builds the LP-fee split.

Steps, type arguments `<Meme, Quote>` throughout:

1. Start the sale:
   - Cetus: `blast_presale::cetus::new(treasury_cap, creation_policy, fee_policy, venue_config,
     cetus_config, pools, tick_spacing)`. It mints the coin's Cetus `PoolCreationCap` from the
     treasury cap, registers the `<Meme, Quote>` pair at `tick_spacing`, and stores the cap in
     `VenueConfig` under `blast_presale::cetus::CreationCapKey`. It records the tier, the tick
     spacing and the fee rate Cetus sets for it, in `VenueConfig` (below). Cetus aborts if it has no fee tier for
     the tick spacing or refuses the pair (the Quote must be in Cetus's permission-pair allowlist
     at that tick spacing).
   - Bluefin: `blast_presale::bluefin::new(treasury_cap, currency, creation_policy, fee_policy,
     venue_config, tick_spacing, pool_fee_rate)`. Tick spacing must be 1..=400 and the fee rate
     1..=20,000 in Bluefin's fee unit (`blast_presale::errors::EInvalidTier`); the coin's symbol
     must be at most 32 bytes (`blast_presale::errors::ESymbolTooLong`). It records the tier in
     `VenueConfig` (below).
   - Aftermath: `blast_presale::aftermath::new<Meme, Quote>(treasury_cap, creation_policy,
     fee_policy, venue_config, dao_fee_bps)`. `dao_fee_bps` is the DAO fee the pool charges on
     every swap, deposit, and withdrawal and pays to the sale's vault, 1..=10,000 BPS
     (`blast_presale::errors::EInvalidDaoFee`); it is the sale's tier, recorded in
     `VenueConfig` (below) with tick spacing 0. The pool's weights and fee are the module's
     constants (50/50, flatness 0, Aftermath's minimum 0.01% swap-in fee, see Migrating to
     Aftermath). The call returns the `PresaleInitializer` and a
     `blast_presale::aftermath::FinalizeTicket<Meme, Quote>`, a hot potato only
     `blast_presale::aftermath::finalize` (step 4) consumes: that call takes the pool-creation
     capability and reserves the sale's pool, and a PTB that finalizes the initializer any other
     way fails with the ticket unconsumed. Beforehand,
     in its own transaction, publish a fresh Aftermath LP coin `Lp` (one per sale, through
     Aftermath's `publish-lp-coin` flow); its publication yields that `CreatePoolCapV2`.

   The pool tier belongs to the venue, not the sale: the `Presale` and `PresaleCreated` carry
   none, and a venue without a tier, such as a vendor's weighted pool, passes none. Cetus and
   Bluefin record a `blast_presale::venue_config::PoolTier` under
   `blast_presale::venue_config::PoolTierKey<Meme>` (each sale token has exactly one sale) and
   emit `blast_presale::venue_config::PoolTierReserved<Meme, Quote, Venue>`, whose third type
   argument is `blast_presale::cetus::Venue`, `blast_presale::bluefin::Venue`, or
   `blast_presale::aftermath::Venue` (tick spacing 0, fee rate the DAO fee in BPS). All three
   then check the `CreationPolicy`, that the sale coin differs from Quote, and that the treasury
   cap has minted nothing; snapshot Blast's current rates from the `FeePolicy`; and return the
   `PresaleInitializer`.
2. Required setters, each taking the initializer by mutable reference:
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_supply(initializer, token_supply, burnable)`.
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_token_allocations(initializer, token_allocation_bps,
     liquidity_token_allocation_bps, recipient_allocations)`.
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_raise(initializer, raise_target, raise_allocations)`.
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_windows(initializer, commitment_duration_ms, liquidity_window_duration_ms)`.
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_eligibility(initializer, eligibility)`.
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_fee_split(initializer, fee_split)`.
3. Optional setters:
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_participant_vesting(initializer, vesting)`: each buyer's tokens vest from
     that buyer's claim. Without it, claims pay tokens out at once.
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_uncapped_phase(initializer, phase)`: lifts wallet caps from the phase's
     start. Without it, caps hold for the whole window.
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_hard_cap(initializer, start_delay_ms, closes_when_filled)`: holds the
     sale to its raise from that point (below). Without it, the sale overflows for its whole window.
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_partner(initializer, creation_policy, partner, clock)`: names a
     `blast_partners::blast_partners::Partner` the `CreationPolicy` currently accepts. This is the only
     time a partner can be named.

   A setter called twice keeps its last value.
4. `blast_presale::blast_presale::finalize(initializer, currency)` first requires confirmed
   `Unregulated` currency status, then checks every setting together, mints the supply,
   consumes the `TreasuryCap`, and returns `(Presale<Meme, Quote>, PresaleCap)`. The Coin Registry
   supply becomes `Fixed`, or `BurnOnly` when `burnable` is true. Emits
   `blast_presale::blast_presale::PresaleCreated`. An Aftermath sale calls
   `blast_presale::aftermath::finalize<Lp, Meme, Quote>(initializer, ticket, currency,
   create_pool_cap)` instead, with the `FinalizeTicket` step 1 returned and the `CreatePoolCapV2`
   of its LP coin `Lp` by value. It consumes the ticket, runs the same finalization, emits
   `blast_presale::aftermath::PoolCreationReserved` (`presale_id`, `pool_creation_id`,
   `create_pool_cap_id`), and returns
   `(Presale<Meme, Quote>, PresaleCap, PoolCreation<Lp, Meme, Quote>)`: the reservation bound to
   the new sale's ID, unshared. It has only `key`, so the same PTB must pass it to
   `blast_presale::aftermath::share` (step 7), which shares it for the migration later. The ticket
   has no abilities and nothing else consumes it, so a PTB that finalizes an Aftermath sale
   through `blast_presale::blast_presale::finalize` fails, and every Aftermath sale carries its
   reservation.
5. Optional, Blast admin only (`FeeAdmin`): `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_protocol_fees` on the pending sale.
6. `blast_presale::blast_presale::share(presale, commitment_starts_at_ms, clock)`, same caller, fixes the windows and shares the
   sale. The start is `max(commitment_starts_at_ms, now)`, so a sale can be published ahead of its start. Emits
   `blast_presale::blast_presale::PresaleOpened`.
7. Aftermath only: `blast_presale::aftermath::share(pool_creation)` shares the reservation
   `finalize` returned; the PTB cannot end holding it.
8. `TransferObjects([presale_cap], creator)`.

Settings:

| Setting | Meaning and rule |
| --- | --- |
| `token_supply` | Whole supply in atomic units, > 0. |
| `burnable` | `true`: supply becomes burn-only; `false`: fixed. |
| `token_allocation_bps` | Buyers' share of the supply, > 0. |
| `liquidity_token_allocation_bps` | Tokens seeded into the pool, > 0. |
| `recipient_allocations` | Up to 64 token recipients, distinct nonzero addresses, each > 0 BPS, optionally vested. Buyers + LP + Blast's token rate + recipients = exactly 10,000 BPS. |
| `participant_vesting` | Optional `VestingTerms` for every buyer's tokens. |
| `raise_target` | Quote the sale must raise, atomic units, > 0. |
| `raise_allocations` | Up to 64 raise recipients paid in Quote at migration, optionally vested. Their BPS plus Blast's raise rate must stay below 10,000; the LP keeps the rest. |
| `duration_ms` | Commitment window length, > 0; set with `commitment_duration_ms`. |
| `liquidity_window_ms` | Time after the window before anyone may cancel an unmigrated funded sale; at least 7 days. |
| `eligibility` | `EligibilityPolicy::Open` or `EligibilityPolicy::Allowlisted` (below). |
| uncapped phase | Optional `blast_presale::blast_presale::UncappedPhase` (below). |
| hard cap | Optional `starts_after_ms` and `closes_when_filled` (below). |
| `fee_split` | `blast_presale::blast_presale::FeeSplit`: up to 16 unvested, distinct LP-fee recipients plus a holder-reward share, totalling exactly 10,000 BPS. The creator takes LP fees by listing itself as a recipient. An empty list with 10,000 holder BPS is valid. |
| `tick_spacing`, `pool_fee_rate` | Pool tier, given to the venue's `new` and kept in `VenueConfig`. Cetus derives the fee rate from the tick spacing. |

A setting never set is zero (supply, raise, window lengths, token BPS), so `finalize` rejects it
with that setting's error. A missing eligibility policy or LP-fee split aborts with
`blast_presale::errors::EMissingSetting`.

Eligibility policies (`blast_presale::blast_presale::EligibilityPolicy`):

- `Open { wallet_cap, max_participants, min_commitment }`: every wallet has the same cap; at most
  `max_participants` distinct wallets (1..=65,536); each wallet's total must reach
  `min_commitment` (0 < min <= cap). `min_commitment × max_participants` must reach the raise
  (`blast_presale::errors::EUnreachableRaise`), so dust wallets cannot fill every slot and block the sale.
- `Allowlisted { root, leaf_count }`: a 32-byte Merkle root over leaves `(index, wallet,
  wallet_cap)`, 1..=65,536 leaves. Caps may be equal, tiered, or custom. Any positive commitment
  counts; there is no minimum.

Uncapped phase (`blast_presale::blast_presale::UncappedPhase`): it starts `starts_after_ms` into the window
(must be below `duration_ms`; zero means from the start) and lifts wallet caps until the end.
Whether the sale then overflows or stops at its raise is the hard cap's job.

- `uncapped_for_eligible`: only wallets the policy admits, with the policy's participant bound
  and, for an open policy, its minimum.
- `uncapped_for_anyone`: any wallet through `blast_presale::blast_presale::commit_uncapped`. `max_participants`
  must be at least the policy's bound (its `max_participants`, or the allowlist's `leaf_count`)
  and at most 65,536. `min_commitment` times the slots held to it must reach the raise: all slots
  under an open policy, only the slots beyond `leaf_count` under an allowlist.

Hard cap (`blast_presale::blast_presale::HardCap`): from `starts_after_ms` into the window (must be below
`duration_ms`, `blast_presale::errors::EInvalidHardCap`), a commitment takes only what is left of the raise and returns
the excess at once; when the raise is full, commitments abort with `blast_presale::errors::EPresaleFilled`. Before that
point the sale overflows. It does not lift wallet caps. Common shapes:

| Shape | Settings |
| --- | --- |
| Overflow for the whole window, pro-rata fill | No hard cap |
| First come, first served within wallet caps | Hard cap at `0` |
| First come, first served without caps | Uncapped phase and hard cap both at `0` |
| Capped overflow round, then a first-come uncapped round | Uncapped phase and hard cap at the same offset |

With `closes_when_filled`, anyone may settle the sale as soon as its raise is full under the hard
cap, without waiting for the window's end (see Settling). Without it, a full sale runs to its
end, so the pool can open at an announced time.

`finalize` aborts unless the LP's tokens and Quote give a seed price both venues can pool
(`blast_presale::errors::EUnseedablePrice`; see Economics).

#### Committing

Who may call: *anyone* the policy admits. The commitment is always credited to the transaction
sender, so a relayer cannot commit for someone else. Each commit returns a `Coin<Quote>`: the part
a hard cap could not accept, or a zero coin. It has no `drop`, so the PTB must transfer it (or
destroy a zero coin).

1. `coin = SplitCoins(source, [amount])`, where `source` is a `Coin<Quote>` the sender owns (the
   gas coin when Quote is SUI and the sender pays gas; under sponsored gas the gas coin is the
   sponsor's).
2. One of, with type arguments `<SaleToken, Quote>`:
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::commit_open(presale, coin, clock)` under an open policy.
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::commit_allowlisted(presale, coin, index, wallet_cap, proof, clock)` under an
     allowlist; `proof` is a `vector<vector<u8>>`. Also used by allowlisted wallets during an
     uncapped phase (the proof is still checked; the cap no longer limits).
   - `blast_presale::blast_presale::commit_uncapped(presale, coin, clock)` once a phase open to anyone has
     started.
3. `TransferObjects([returned_coin], sender)`.

Each commit emits `blast_presale::blast_presale::Committed`. Rules:

- The window is `start_ms <= now < end_ms`.
- A wallet's first commit takes a participant slot; later commits top it up by any positive
  amount. The minimum applies to the wallet's total after the commit, so the first commit must
  reach it. The commit that exactly fills a hard cap may be below the minimum.
- Before the uncapped phase, the wallet's total must stay within its cap. The cap a wallet first
  committed under is stored with its commitment; under an allowlist, later commits must present
  the same cap (`blast_presale::errors::EInvalidEligibilityProof`).
- Under an open policy, `commit_open` keeps working in either uncapped phase: caps are lifted,
  its minimum still applies, and an anyone-phase uses the phase's participant bound.

#### Allowlist proofs

Leaf digest, for the wallet at position `index` with cap `wallet_cap`:

```
leaf = blake2b256( b"\x00blast-presale-v1"            // 0x00 then the ASCII bytes
                   || bcs(index: u64)                  // 8 bytes, little-endian
                   || bcs(wallet: address)             // 32 bytes
                   || bcs(wallet_cap: u64) )           // 8 bytes, little-endian
node(left, right) = blake2b256( 0x01 || left || right )
```

The proof is positional: starting from the leaf digest with `i = index`, for each sibling in
order, `digest = node(digest, sibling)` when `i` is even, else `node(sibling, digest)`; then
`i = i / 2`. The result must equal the root. The proof must contain exactly
`ceil(log2(leaf_count))` siblings (zero for one leaf, where the root is the leaf itself), each 32
bytes, and `index < leaf_count`. The verifier takes each sibling as given, so the tree builder
picks one rule for an unpaired node at an odd-width level (for example, pairing it with itself)
and puts that sibling in the proof. The `wallet` in the leaf must be the transaction sender, and
`wallet_cap` must be positive.

#### Settling

Who may call: *anyone*. `blast_presale::blast_presale::settle(presale, clock)` while `Open`, once either:

- `now >= end_ms`; or
- the sale closes early: its hard cap has `closes_when_filled`, the hard cap is in force
  (`now >= start_ms + hard cap starts_after_ms`), and `total_commitments >= raise_target`. The
  sale can then take no more Quote.

If total commitments reach the raise the sale becomes `Funded` and emits
`blast_presale::blast_presale::PresaleFunded`; otherwise it becomes `Cancelled` and emits
`blast_presale::blast_presale::PresaleCancelled`. Closing early ends the window at the settle: the
stored `duration_ms` becomes the time the sale ran, so `end_ms` and the LP deadline count from the
close. `PresaleFunded` carries both. A sale without a hard cap never closes early.

Closing early and migrating can run in one PTB: `settle`, then the venue's `migrate`. Because
migration is permissionless, the wallet whose commitment fills the raise can also commit, settle,
migrate, and buy from the new pool in one transaction. The pool's seed price is the same either
way; creators who want a public start choose `closes_when_filled = false`.

#### Migrating to Cetus

Who may call: *anyone*, while `Funded`, until someone cancels. Usually one keeper PTB:

1. `blast_presale::blast_presale::settle(presale, clock)` if not yet settled.
2. `blast_presale::cetus::migrate<Meme, Quote, CoinA, CoinB>(sale, fee_policy, venue_config,
   cetus_config, pools, burn_manager, clock)`. `CoinA` and `CoinB` are the
   sale's two types in Cetus's canonical order: the order Cetus's own `is_right_order` check (in
   its `factory` module) accepts. Find it by dev-inspecting either order; the wrong order aborts
   with `blast_presale::errors::EInvalidCoinOrder`, and a pair that is not exactly the sale's two
   types aborts with `blast_presale::errors::EWrongCoinPair`. Shared objects: the presale
   (`sale`), `FeePolicy`, `VenueConfig` (read), Cetus `GlobalConfig` (`cetus_config`, read),
   Cetus `Pools` (mutable), and the Cetus LP-burn `BurnManager` (mutable).
3. On a partnered sale, `blast_presale::blast_presale::pay_protocol_fees_with_partner(presale, fee_policy,
   partner)`.

Migration calls `blast_presale::blast_presale::migrate`, which pays Blast (or holds its fees on a partnered
sale), pays or vests each raise recipient, pays or vests each token recipient, and returns the
LP's tokens and Quote. The adapter creates the pool with the reserved `PoolCreationCap` at the
tick spacing `new` recorded in `VenueConfig`, seeds a full-range position at the price the LP balances imply, burns the
position through Cetus LP-burn for its fee-claiming proof, and shares a new `Vault` holding
that proof and whatever the pool did not take. Nothing returns to the caller. Any venue failure
rolls the whole transition back.

#### Migrating to Bluefin

Who may call: *anyone*, while `Funded`, until someone cancels.

1. `blast_presale::blast_presale::settle(presale, clock)` if not yet settled.
2. `creation_fee = SplitCoins(GasCoin, [amount])`, where `amount` is the fee amount (the `u64` in
   the `(bool, u64)` pair) that Bluefin's `get_pool_creation_fee_amount<SUI>` (its `config`
   module) returns at submission time; Bluefin rejects another amount.
3. `blast_presale::bluefin::migrate<Meme, Quote>(sale, fee_policy, venue_config, currency,
   quote_currency, bluefin_config, creation_fee, clock)`. `venue_config` is the shared
   `VenueConfig` (read for the tier `new` recorded). `currency` and `quote_currency` are the
   shared Coin Registry `Currency<Meme>` and `Currency<Quote>` (read for both symbols and decimals
   and the Quote's icon URL); the Bluefin `GlobalConfig` (`bluefin_config`) is mutable.
4. On a partnered sale, `blast_presale::blast_presale::pay_protocol_fees_with_partner(...)`.

The adapter creates the pool `Pool<Meme, Quote>` (Meme is always coin A) named
`<Meme symbol>-<Quote symbol>` at the recorded tier, opens a full-range position aligned inward to
the tick spacing, adds the LP balances, moves the position into a new shared `Vault`, and
shares the pool.

#### Migrating to Aftermath

Who may call: *anyone*, while `Funded`, until someone cancels.

1. `blast_presale::blast_presale::settle(presale, clock)` if not yet settled.
2. `blast_presale::aftermath::migrate<Lp, Meme, Quote>(sale, pool_creation, fee_policy,
   venue_config, pool_registry, dao_fee_version, clock)`. `pool_creation` is the sale's
   `PoolCreation<Lp, Meme, Quote>` (shared by `blast_presale::aftermath::share`), passed by value
   and deleted; another sale's aborts with
   `blast_presale::errors::EWrongPresale` before anything else. `venue_config` is the shared
   `VenueConfig` (read for the DAO fee `new` recorded); `pool_registry` is Aftermath's shared
   `PoolRegistry` (mutable); `dao_fee_version` is the DAO-fee package's shared `Version`. The
   module sorts the coins into Aftermath's order itself.
3. On a partnered sale, `blast_presale::blast_presale::pay_protocol_fees_with_partner(...)`.

The adapter runs `blast_presale::blast_presale::migrate`, creates the pool from all LP tokens
and Quote (50/50 weights, flatness 0, Aftermath's minimum 0.01% swap-in fee, which compounds
into the LP, no other pool fees, name "Blast Presale Pool"; no sale token circulates before the
migration, so nobody can register the sale's pool first), checks it holds every unit
(`blast_presale::errors::EPoolMismatch`), builds the `Vault` with no position yet, wraps the
pool in a DAO-fee pool at the recorded `dao_fee_bps` whose fee recipient is the vault's ID
(`blast_presale::errors::EDaoFeePoolMismatch` if Aftermath reports anything else), attaches
the DAO-fee pool's `OwnerCap` as the vault's position with the LP coin's amount (the pool's whole
liquidity) as its `position_liquidity`, shares the vault, shares the DAO-fee pool (the object traders
use), and sends the LP coin to `0x0`, where nobody can ever use it. Emits
`blast_presale::aftermath::DaoFeePoolCreated` with the vault, base pool, DAO-fee pool, owner cap,
and LP coin IDs before `presale_vault::VaultCreated`, whose `pool_id` is the base pool and
`position_id` the owner cap. Nothing in the package borrows or removes the owner cap, so the fee
or its recipient cannot be changed, and the liquidity is locked for good. If the
`CreatePoolCapV2` belongs to a different LP coin than `Lp`, or Aftermath retires the versions
this package links to, migration aborts and the sale becomes refundable at its LP deadline.

#### Locking your own position without a presale

Who may call: *anyone*, with their own position. A team that adds liquidity to Cetus or Bluefin
itself, without a presale, can lock that position for good in a `Vault`, which then splits
its LP fees exactly as a migrated sale's vault does: Blast's LP-fee share first, then the team's
`FeeSplit` between its fee recipients and holder-reward rounds.

1. Create the pool and open and fund the position with the venue's own calls; keep whatever the
   venue did not take.
2. `fee_split = blast_presale::blast_presale::fee_split(...)`, as for a presale.
3. Cetus: `blast_presale::cetus::new_vault<Meme, Quote, CoinA, CoinB>(position,
   fee_split, partner_id, creation_policy, fee_policy, pool, burn_manager, clock)`, where `pool` is the
   `Pool<CoinA, CoinB>` holding the position (read) and `CoinA` and `CoinB` are Meme and Quote in
   the pool's order. The position is burned through Cetus LP-burn for its fee-claiming proof,
   which Cetus's `BurnManager` (mutable) issues only for positions it accepts.
   Bluefin: `blast_presale::bluefin::new_vault<Meme, Quote>(position, fee_split, partner_id,
   creation_policy, fee_policy, pool, clock)`, where `pool` is the `Pool<Meme, Quote>` holding the
   position (read); a pool whose first coin is not Meme is not supported.

The `CreationPolicy` must allow Quote and the venue's migrator witness, the same check a presale
passes. The vault snapshots the `FeePolicy`'s current LP-fee rates. It names no presale: its
`presale_id` and `presale_cap_id` are the zero ID, so no `PresaleCap` claims from it, and it holds
no residuals. `partner_id` (an `Option<ID>`) optionally names a Blast partner, which the
`CreationPolicy` must accept now (`blast_presale::errors::EPartnerNotAccepted` otherwise) and the vault
keeps for good; Blast's LP fees are then held for `presale_vault::pay_protocol_lp_fees_with_partner`,
as on a partnered sale's vault, and the partner earns only its cut of them. A position from another pool aborts with
`blast_presale::errors::EPositionPoolMismatch` or `blast_presale::errors::EPositionPoolMismatch`;
a position with no liquidity aborts with `blast_presale::errors::EZeroLiquidity`. Fees are then collected
with the venue's `collect_fees`, and holder-reward rounds work as for any vault.

#### Paying a partnered sale's Blast fees

Who may call: *anyone*, once, after migration. `blast_presale::blast_presale::pay_protocol_fees_with_partner(presale,
fee_policy, partner)` takes the Blast raise fee the migration held, pays the partner its
cut through `blast_partners::blast_partners::pay`, then pays Blast the rest of the raise fee and its whole token
fee at the `FeePolicy`'s current destination. Emits `blast_partners::blast_partners::PartnerPaid` (when the cut is
positive) and `blast_presale::blast_presale::ProtocolFeesPaid`. The partner is paid as an owned coin at its
recipient address using `public_transfer`.

#### Claiming tokens and refunds

Who may call: *anyone* may relay; payment always goes to `participant`.
`blast_presale::blast_presale::claim(presale, participant, clock)` while `Migrated` or `Cancelled`. Batch many
claims in one PTB. It removes the wallet's commitment record, so each wallet claims once.

- `Migrated`: pays the wallet's pro-rata tokens and its share of the overflow refund.
- `Cancelled`: pays back the full commitment; no tokens.
- With participant vesting, the tokens go into a new shared, irrevocable schedule for the
  participant that starts at this claim; the Quote refund is always paid at once. A claim whose
  token amount is zero creates no schedule.

Emits `blast_presale::blast_presale::Claimed` with `tokens`, `quote_refund`, `remaining_participants`, and
`vesting_id`.

#### Claiming vested tokens

Vested raise shares (Quote) and token shares start at migration; vested participant tokens start
at the participant's claim. Each schedule is a shared `Vesting<T>` from the immutable
`blast_fun_vesting` package, with a fixed beneficiary and no cancellation authority. Find its ID
in the `vesting_id` field of `blast_presale::blast_presale::RaiseAllocated`, `blast_presale::blast_presale::RecipientAllocated`,
or `blast_presale::blast_presale::Claimed`.

- Claim: `blast_fun_linear_vesting::claim<T>(vesting, clock)`. *Anyone* may call; it transfers all
  newly vested value to the beneficiary as a coin and aborts with
  `blast_fun_linear_vesting::ENothingClaimable` when nothing new has vested.
- Vested amount at time `t`: zero before `start + cliff_ms`; the whole amount from
  `start + period_ms × periods`; otherwise `floor(total × floor((t − start) / period_ms) / periods)`.
  The cliff only gates: once it passes, every whole period since the start counts.
- `blast_fun_linear_vesting::close_irrevocable<T>(vesting)` deletes a drained schedule; anyone.

#### Cancelling an unlaunched sale and refunds

Who may call: *anyone*. `blast_presale::blast_presale::cancel_unlaunched(presale, clock)` once `now >=
end_ms + liquidity_window_ms` while `Funded`. The sale becomes `Cancelled` and emits
`blast_presale::blast_presale::PresaleCancelled`. Every wallet then claims a full refund with
`blast_presale::blast_presale::claim`. A sale nobody settled can be settled and cancelled in one PTB after the
LP deadline. All minted tokens stay locked in the cancelled sale forever.

#### Collecting LP fees

Who may call: *anyone*. Each collection pays Blast (or, on a partnered vault, holds Blast's part)
and every fee recipient at once. It pays the holder Meme remainder to the governed
`FeePolicy` destination and retains holder Quote in the vault. Shared objects only; nothing returns.

- Cetus: `blast_presale::cetus::collect_fees<Meme, Quote, CoinA, CoinB>(vault, fee_policy,
  cetus_config, burn_manager, pool)` where `pool` is the vault's
  `Pool<CoinA, CoinB>` (same coin order as migration; another pool aborts with
  `blast_presale::errors::EPositionPoolMismatch`).
- Bluefin: `blast_presale::bluefin::collect_fees<Meme, Quote>(vault, fee_policy, bluefin_config,
  pool, clock)` where `pool` is the vault's `Pool<Meme, Quote>`
  (`blast_presale::errors::EPositionPoolMismatch` otherwise).
- Aftermath: `blast_presale::aftermath::collect_fees<Meme, Quote>(vault, fee_policy, meme_fees,
  quote_fees)`, on an Aftermath vault only (`blast_presale::errors::ENotAftermathVault` otherwise).
  Aftermath pays the DAO fee of every swap, deposit, and withdrawal as a separate `Coin<Meme>` or
  `Coin<Quote>` sent to the vault's address, so the vault owns those coins.
  `meme_fees` and `quote_fees` are `vector<Receiving<Coin<Meme>>>` and
  `vector<Receiving<Coin<Quote>>>`: list the IDs of the coins the vault owns (query the vault
  address's owned objects) as PTB receiving inputs and gather each list with `MakeMoveVec`;
  either list may be empty. The call receives every listed coin into the vault, joins them, and
  splits the totals exactly as the other venues split a collected position's fees. A coin the
  vault does not own aborts in `sui::transfer`; a coin left unlisted waits for a later call.

Emits `presale_vault::FeesCollected`, followed by `presale_vault::HolderMemePaid`
when the holder Meme remainder is positive. The former records allocation; the latter
records the payment to the treasury. The vault keeps no holder Meme, so rounds pay only
Quote. A collection of zero is valid and emits nothing. Neither
adapter collects venue incentive rewards.

On a partnered vault, follow with `presale_vault::pay_protocol_lp_fees_with_partner(vault,
fee_policy, partner)`: *anyone*; it pays the partner its cut of each held asset and Blast
the rest, emitting `presale_vault::ProtocolLpFeesPaid` and `blast_partners::blast_partners::PartnerPaid`. Holding
nothing is valid and emits nothing, so it can follow every collection.

#### Migration residuals and the PresaleCap

- `presale_vault::claim_migration_residuals(vault, presale_cap)`: *cap holder* (`PresaleCap`).
  Returns `(Coin<Meme>, Coin<Quote>)` holding what the pool did not take when it was seeded;
  transfer both in the same PTB. Aborts with `blast_presale::errors::ENoMigrationResiduals` when both are
  empty, so it works once. Emits `presale_vault::MigrationResidualsClaimed`.
- `blast_presale::blast_presale::destroy_cap(presale, presale_cap)`: *cap holder*, only when the sale is
  `Cancelled`. A migrated sale's cap cannot be destroyed.

#### Holder-reward rounds

The holder Quote share of LP fees accrues in the vault. Blast decides off chain
who receives holder assets and whether each round reimburses gas. A single
`blast_presale::holder_rewards::Round` holds its holder balances separately from its optional
Quote gas reserve.

1. `blast_presale::holder_rewards::schedule_round`: *Blast admin* (`RewardsAdmin`). It takes the
   mutable shared vault, the round number, checkpoint interval, root and
   manifest digest, leaf count, exact holder Meme/Quote amounts, an explicit gas
   reserve amount, the claim window in milliseconds, the expected treasury
   address and Clock. The terms' own checks run first: root and manifest digest
   are 32 bytes, with 1..=65,536 leaves, a zero Meme amount
   (`blast_presale::errors::EMemeRewardsUnsupported`: holder Meme fees go to the treasury,
   and the field stays for parity with the migrators' leaf), a positive holder
   Quote budget, a nonempty
   checkpoint interval, a holder Quote plus reserve that fits in a `u64`, a
   reserve of at most 10% of the holder Quote
   (`blast_presale::errors::EGasReserveTooLarge`), a nonzero expected treasury and a
   positive claim window. Then, to fail fast,
   the number must be the vault's next round (starting at zero), the interval
   must start at or after the previous round ended (skipped periods need no
   funded round or number), and holder Quote plus reserve must fit the
   vault's unreserved holder Quote. The round waits in the vault's
   `round_publication` slot until the applied round notice elapses; nothing is
   reserved yet. Scheduling again replaces it (or a pending notice change) and
   restarts the notice. It emits `delayed_action::ActionScheduled` with key
   `presale_vault::RoundPublicationKey` and `change = Action(RoundTerms)`, so
   the terms are public while the round waits.
2. `blast_presale::holder_rewards::publish_round`: *anyone*, once the scheduled round is
   ready. It takes the mutable shared vault, shared governed `FeePolicy` and
   Clock, and nothing else. It consumes the scheduled round, then re-checks that
   the expected treasury still equals the governed destination
   (`blast_presale::errors::ETreasuryChanged` rejects a policy change after scheduling)
   and that the number, interval and budget still fit the vault. The claim
   deadline is the publication time plus the claim window
   (`blast_presale::errors::EClaimDeadlineOverflow` if it exceeds `u64`), so a late
   publication still gets the full window. It snapshots the checked treasury
   and emits `delayed_action::ActionApplied`, then `blast_presale::holder_rewards::RoundPublished`
   with the absolute deadline. Zero reserve disables reimbursement for this
   round and requires no settlement. A positive reserve creates separate
   pending custody. Blast may cover gas and allocate the entire holder Quote
   budget to holder leaves. The round notice starts at two hours, so a round is
   public and cancellable before it publishes; a daily cadence publishes each
   round before scheduling the next, since a new schedule replaces a waiting one.
3. `blast_presale::holder_rewards::cancel_round`: *Blast admin* (`CancelAdmin`). It discards
   the scheduled round, even a ready one, and emits
   `delayed_action::ActionCancelled` with its terms. Nothing was reserved, so no
   balance moves. `blast_presale::errors::EWrongRoundProposal` rejects it while a notice
   change is pending instead.
4. Round notice: `blast_presale::holder_rewards::schedule_round_delay` (*Blast admin*,
   `RewardsAdmin`) proposes a new notice, ready after the applied one and
   replacing any scheduled round; `blast_presale::holder_rewards::apply_round_delay` (*anyone*)
   applies it once ready; `blast_presale::holder_rewards::cancel_round_delay` (*Blast admin*,
   `CancelAdmin`) discards it (`blast_presale::errors::EWrongRoundProposal` while a
   round is scheduled instead). A shorter notice, zero included, still waits the
   applied one. Every vault starts with a 7,200,000 ms (2-hour) notice; no notice
   exceeds `blast_admin::delayed::max_delay_ms` (30 days).
5. `blast_presale::holder_rewards::claim`: *anyone* may relay, while `now < claim_deadline_ms`
   (`blast_presale::errors::EClaimsClosed` from the deadline, so claims never race
   `close_round`). It takes the mutable shared round, beneficiary/amount proof
   and Clock, and pays that beneficiary only, once per index. It emits `blast_presale::holder_rewards::RewardClaimed` and leaves gas custody
   untouched. Leaf:

   ```
   blake2b256( b"\x00blast-presale-holder-rewards-v1"
               || bcs(vault_id: ID)        // 32 bytes
               || bcs(round_number: u64) || bcs(index: u64)
               || bcs(beneficiary: address)
               || bcs(meme_amount: u64) || bcs(quote_amount: u64) )
   ```

   The proof follows the allowlist rules above (same node hash, positional
   order, exact depth).
6. `blast_presale::holder_rewards::settle_gas_reserve`: *Blast admin* (`RewardsAdmin`). It takes
   the mutable shared round and its mutable shared vault and an amount from
   zero through an enabled reserve. It pays the publication-time treasury,
   returns all unused Quote to the vault and consumes settlement once.
   `blast_presale::holder_rewards::GasReserveSettled` records payment, return and remaining
   vault Quote. Disabled reimbursement and repeated settlement abort. The
   contract bounds custody; verified off-chain effects determine actual cost.
7. `blast_presale::holder_rewards::close_round`: *anyone*, once `now >= claim_deadline_ms`.
   It consumes the shared round and returns unclaimed holder assets and any
   unsettled reserve to the correct mutable vault. It emits
   `blast_presale::holder_rewards::RoundClosed` and deletes the round. Missing settlement
   authority cannot strand reserve. Elapsed time alone moves nothing.
   Closing before reimbursement leaves that cost with Blast.

#### Blast admin operations

Integrators cannot call these; they explain state changes. Each takes the
`blast_acl::AdminWitness` of the role listed in "Objects and authority" (*Blast admin*).

| Call | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `fee_policy::schedule_fees` | Rates new sales snapshot. Raise and token rates at most 1,000 BPS each; each LP-fee rate at most 3,000 (`blast_presale::errors::EInvalidFees`). Compiled maximums: raising one needs a package upgrade. Application emits `delayed::DelayedApplied<fee_policy::FeesKey, fee_policy::ProtocolFees>`. |
| `fee_policy::schedule_destination` | Redirects every later Blast payout, existing sales included; rejects `0x0`. Application emits `delayed::DelayedApplied<fee_policy::DestinationKey, address>`. |
| `blast_presale::blast_presale::set_protocol_fees` | Takes the live `FeePolicy`; each proposed rate must be at or below its applied rate. Replaces one sale's four rates in its creation PTB before `share` (`Pending`), where a rate may rise, or while `Open` and before `start_ms`, where each rate may only stay or fall (`blast_presale::errors::EProtocolFeesIncreased` otherwise). Emits `blast_presale::blast_presale::ProtocolFeesChanged`. |
| `presale_vault::schedule_protocol_lp_fees` | Replaces one vault's Blast LP-fee rates for later collections, each at most 3,000 BPS (`blast_presale::errors::EInvalidFees`). Application emits `delayed::DelayedApplied<presale_vault::ProtocolLpFeesKey, fee_policy::ProtocolFees>`. |
| `creation_policy::set_quote_allowed` | Allows or disallows a Quote type for later sales. Emits `creation_policy::QuoteSet`. |
| `creation_policy::schedule_migration_witness` | Schedules admission of a migrator witness; rejects primitives, vectors, and `0x1`/`0x2` types. Application emits `delayed_set::SetApplied<creation_policy::MigrationWitnessKey, TypeName>`; `remove_migration_witness` removes immediately (emitting `delayed_set::MemberRemoved` for an admitted witness) and cancels pending admission. |
| `creation_policy::add_partner` | Lets new sales name a partner at once (also cancels a pending removal). Emits `creation_policy::PartnerAdded`. |
| `creation_policy::remove_partner` | New sales may still name the partner for `blast_partners::blast_partners::delay_ms` (7 days). Sales that already name it keep paying it. Emits `creation_policy::PartnerRemoved`. |
| `blast_presale::holder_rewards::schedule_round`, `blast_presale::holder_rewards::schedule_round_delay`, `blast_presale::holder_rewards::cancel_round`, `blast_presale::holder_rewards::cancel_round_delay`, `blast_presale::holder_rewards::settle_gas_reserve` | See above. |
| `blast_presale::package_admin::authorize_upgrade`, `blast_presale::package_admin::commit_upgrade_and_advance` | Compatible upgrades with atomic operational-version cutover. |

`blast_presale::package_admin::wrap` consumes the publication Publication and never-upgraded matching cap once. Each upgrade increments both compiled generation constants and commits/advances in one PTB; old bytecode then rejects the advanced version. Existing dependency-only deployments require a fresh publication to adopt this design.

### Delayed administration

Each treasury, fee or upgrade operation owns its applied notice period. A delayed-value
schedule accepts a proposed value and **next** `delay_ms`, but its execution deadline is
`ready_at_ms = now + currently_applied_delay_ms`. Passing zero cannot shorten the
current wait. The proposed value and next notice become active together only after
explicit application with the current version and canonical Clock. A value-only
change supplies the applied delay; a delay-only change supplies the applied value.
Different operations, including operations in the same package, can use different delays.

Rescheduling replaces the proposal and restarts the full currently applied notice.
`CancelAdmin` can cancel even a ready proposal, preserving the applied value and delay.
Ordinary value applications need no role; code authorization and immutability execution
still need UpgradeAdmin. Overflow is rejected at scheduling and actual application;
later schedules check their own timestamp addition too. A value proposal that changes neither
value nor notice, or a notice-only proposal equal to the applied notice, aborts with code 20
(`EUnchanged`) from Blast admin's `delayed` module (`delayed_action` for the upgrade notice,
`delayed_set` for the admission notice).
Read the live notice before relying on a cancellation window.

Each delayed field is a Blast admin delayed value: a `delayed::Delayed` setting, the
`delayed_action::DelayedAction` upgrade slot, or the `delayed_set::DelayedSet` of adapters. The
module of each type emits every schedule, cancel and apply event; the presale package emits none
of its own. The events are generic in the operation's key and value type and carry `owner` (the
ID of the object that stores the field) and `key`. A value schedule emits
`delayed::DelayedScheduled` (after `delayed::DelayedCancelled` for a replaced proposal), a cancel
emits `delayed::DelayedCancelled`, and an application emits `delayed::DelayedApplied` with the
previous and new value and the applied notice. Creating a setting emits
`delayed::DelayedCreated` (so creating a vault emits it for the vault's two fields), the upgrade
slot and each vault's round-publication slot `delayed_action::ActionCreated`, and the admission set
`delayed_set::SetCreated`. Upgrade actions, scheduled holder-reward rounds, and their notice
changes emit `delayed_action::ActionScheduled`,
`delayed_action::ActionCancelled` and `delayed_action::ActionApplied`, whose `change` is
`Action(...)` or `Delay` (a notice change). Adapter admissions and their notice changes emit
`delayed_set::SetScheduled`, `delayed_set::SetCancelled` and `delayed_set::SetApplied`, whose
`change` is `Admission(...)` or `Delay`. Their `delay_ms` is the proposed next notice for a
notice change and the applied notice for an action or admission. `delayed_set::MemberRemoved`
records an immediate adapter removal.

| Operation | Object and field | Key | Value or action type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Blast's rates | `FeePolicy.fees` | `fee_policy::FeesKey` | `fee_policy::ProtocolFees` |
| Blast's payee | `FeePolicy.destination` | `fee_policy::DestinationKey` | `address` |
| A vault's Blast LP-fee rates | `Vault.protocol_fees` | `presale_vault::ProtocolLpFeesKey` | `fee_policy::ProtocolFees` |
| A vault's creator split | `Vault.fee_split` | `presale_vault::FeeSplitKey` | `blast_presale::blast_presale::FeeSplit` |
| A vault's next holder-reward round and the round notice | `Vault.round_publication` | `presale_vault::RoundPublicationKey` | `presale_vault::RoundTerms` |
| Upgrades and immutability | `PackageAdmin.upgrade` | `blast_presale::package_admin::UpgradeKey` | `blast_presale::package_admin::UpgradeAction` |
| Adapter admissions | `CreationPolicy.migration_witnesses` | `creation_policy::MigrationWitnessKey` | `TypeName` |

`blast_presale::package_admin::schedule_upgrade` takes only the digest in addition to
its state, authority and Clock inputs, and uses the stored upgrade notice.
`blast_presale::package_admin::authorize_upgrade` consumes only a ready matching digest;
its ticket must feed the native upgrade command and its receipt the ordinary finalizer.
`blast_presale::package_admin::schedule_make_immutable` and
`blast_presale::package_admin::make_immutable` govern destruction of upgrade authority.
These action schedules accept no delay argument and their execution preserves the notice.
`blast_presale::package_admin::schedule_upgrade_delay` uses UpgradeAdmin to propose only the
notice period, replacing any pending action. Anyone applies it with
`blast_presale::package_admin::apply_upgrade_delay`; it cannot authorize code or immutability.
`blast_presale::package_admin::cancel_upgrade_action` cancels any of these proposals.

Publication-owned policy singletons start with zero notice for ordinary
role-authorized setup; package upgrade custody starts at 172,800,000 ms (48 hours), so
no upgrade or immutability action can run without notice, even during setup. Configure
and apply each other operation's intended notice, and drain or cancel all earlier setup
proposals before release. `blast_presale::package_admin::unpause` enforces the minimum: it
aborts unless the fee destination, fee rates and adapter set each have a nonzero applied
notice, no pending proposal that would set one to zero, and no pending adapter admission. Raising a notice never changes previously scheduled deadlines or next delays.
Pausing and upgrades cannot reset notices. This source requires a fresh stack.

Adapter admissions share one applied notice across witness types, held in the
`delayed_set::DelayedSet` `CreationPolicy.migration_witnesses`; a fresh type cannot reopen setup.
`creation_policy::schedule_migration_witness` accepts only the witness type in addition to its state, authority and Clock inputs. It snapshots
the applied notice and deadline; application only admits that witness and preserves the
live notice. `creation_policy::schedule_migration_delay` proposes a new notice under
AdapterAdmin; anyone calls `creation_policy::apply_migration_delay`, and CancelAdmin uses
`creation_policy::cancel_migration_delay`. Applying admissions before or after a policy
change cannot overwrite that policy. Existing admission deadlines remain fixed; settle
or cancel all zero-notice admissions before completing setup. Immediate adapter removal
cancels that type's pending admission and preserves the applied notice. Scheduling an
admitted witness, or removing one that is neither admitted nor pending, aborts with code 20
from `delayed_set`.

New vaults start their own LP-fee notice at 48 hours; creating a fresh vault never
reopens zero-notice setup. Vault fee changes can propose a different next notice,
which waits the vault's currently applied notice.

### Emergency pause

A `PauseAdmin` calls `blast_presale_package::pause` to set selected bits on the shared
package version. Only `UnpauseAdmin` may clear bits, with `blast_presale::package_admin::unpause`,
which takes the shared PackageAdmin, PackageVersion, FeePolicy and CreationPolicy and first checks
that every policy notice is guarded (see above).
CREATE is 1, BUY is 2, MIGRATE is 8.
Pauses never expire. Claims, refunds and mandatory settlement remain callable.
Presale creation/sharing, all three commitment paths and migration check their respective bits; claim, cancel_unlaunched and settle stay open.

`blast_presale::blast_presale::set_protocol_fees` remains immediate before the
sale starts, but now takes the live `FeePolicy`; every rate must be at or below
its applied rates. Scheduled increases cannot authorize larger sale overrides.
Once a sale is shared it is public, so an override there may only keep or lower
each of its four rates; only the creation PTB may raise one.
AdapterAdmin may immediately remove an adapter with `creation_policy::remove_migration_witness`.
Genesis treasury is configured before publication, never defaulted to the publisher.

### Economics

Publication defaults follow the [Blast visual map](https://map.blast.fun/#fees): 200 BPS (2%) of the successful raise target, 100 BPS (1%) of total Meme supply, and 1,500 BPS (15%) of each collected LP-fee asset. Administrators can change the policy; sales snapshot their rates. Changing source defaults does not update an existing policy, sale or vault.

All amounts are atomic units. All rates are BPS out of 10,000. `floor` rounds down.

#### Largest-remainder apportionment

Supply, raise, and every LP-fee split use one method. For shares `s_i` summing to 10,000 and a
total `X`: each share gets `floor(X × s_i / 10,000)`; the leftover units (fewer than the number of
shares) go one each to the shares with the largest remainder `(X × s_i) mod 10,000`; ties go to
the earlier share. Every unit lands in exactly one share.

- Supply, at creation, in order: buyers (`token_allocation_bps`), LP, Blast (`token_bps`), then
  token recipients in list order. Buyers, LP, and every recipient must get > 0
  (`blast_presale::errors::EInvalidTokenAllocation`); Blast may get 0.
- Raise, at creation, in order: raise recipients, Blast (`raise_bps`), then the LP with
  `10,000 − recipients − Blast`. Every recipient and the LP must get > 0
  (`blast_presale::errors::EInvalidRaiseAllocation`).
- These amounts are fixed at creation, except that a per-sale rate change before the start
  replaces Blast's amounts (below). Migration pays them from exactly `raise_target`; the LP
  Quote is `raise_target − Blast's Quote − raise recipients' Quote`.

#### Fill rate, claims, and dust

Let `T` be total commitments, `R` the raise target, `A` the buyers' token allocation, and `c` one
wallet's commitment. A migrated sale requires `T >= R`. The common fill rate is `R / T`.

- Tokens: `floor(A × c / T)`.
- Overflow refund: `floor((T − R) × c / T)`.
- Cancelled sale: refund `floor(T × c / T) = c`; no tokens.
- The last wallet to claim, whichever it is, takes everything left of the tokens and Quote
  instead, so no rounding dust is stranded. Its extra is under one atomic unit per other
  claimant, per asset.
- Buyers together pay `R` for `A` tokens: the presale price is `R / A` Quote per atomic token.
  The pool opens at `LP Quote / LP tokens`.

Worked example: supply 20,001 at 5,000 / 1,000 / 0 / 2,500 / 1,500 BPS (buyers, LP, Blast,
recipient A, recipient B) apportions to 10,001 / 2,000 / 0 / 5,000 / 3,000 (the buyers' 0.5
remainder is the largest). Raise 1,000; Alice commits 1,000 and Bob 3,000, so `T = 4,000`. Alice
claims first: `floor(10,001 × 1,000 / 4,000) = 2,500` tokens and `floor(3,000 × 1,000 / 4,000) =
750` Quote. Bob claims last and takes the rest: 7,501 tokens and 2,250 Quote.

When the raise fills under a hard cap, `T` equals `R` and every refund is zero. If the sale
already overflowed before its hard cap started, the hard cap accepts nothing (`blast_presale::errors::EPresaleFilled`)
and the earlier overflow fills pro rata as usual.

#### Blast's fees

Blast takes three fees, all from the sale's snapshot (`Presale.protocol_fees`), copied from
`FeePolicy` at creation. Later `fee_policy::schedule_fees` calls never touch existing sales. Nothing is
charged at creation, on commitment, on refund, or when a sale does not migrate.

- Raise fee: Blast's Quote, apportioned with the raise at creation, paid at migration. Overflow
  refunds are never charged.
- Token fee: Blast's tokens, apportioned with the supply at creation, paid at migration.
- LP fees: at each collection, Blast takes `ceil(gross × lp_fee_meme_bps / 10,000)` of the Meme
  and `ceil(gross × lp_fee_quote_bps / 10,000)` of the Quote (rounded up), at the vault's current
  rates. The vault starts with the sale's snapshot rates; `presale_vault::schedule_protocol_lp_fees`
  can change them later, never above 3,000 BPS.
- Every payout goes to `FeePolicy.destination` as it is when paid.

Per-sale changes before the start (`blast_presale::blast_presale::set_protocol_fees`): a rate may rise
only in the creation PTB; on a shared sale each rate may only stay or fall. A changed raise rate
becomes `floor(R × raise_bps / 10,000)` and takes from or gives to the LP's Quote; a changed token
rate becomes `floor(supply × token_bps / 10,000)` and takes from or gives to the buyers'
allocation `A`. A rate equal to the sale's current one keeps its current amount (the creation
amount unless an earlier change replaced it). Recipients keep their amounts. The
new amounts must leave the LP some Quote and the buyers some tokens, and the LP must still seed a
poolable price.

#### Partners

A sale may name one `blast_partners::blast_partners::Partner`, named on the initializer and fixed
at `finalize`. The partner earns a cut of Blast's raise fee and of Blast's LP fees, never of Blast's
token fee. The cut is
`floor(fee × share_bps / 10,000)` using the partner's share applied when paid (at most 8,000
BPS; a change Blast proposes can be applied by anyone 7 days later). Blast keeps the rest. On a
partnered sale, migration holds Blast's raise fee and tokens in the sale, and each collection
holds Blast's LP fees in the vault, until the two pay calls run.

#### LP-fee split

After Blast's LP fees, the rest of each asset is apportioned by largest remainder over the fee
recipients in order, then the holder-reward share. Ties favor fee recipients over holders and
earlier recipients over later ones. Recipients are paid as coins in the same transaction (a zero
amount sends nothing); holder Quote stays in the vault for rounds and holder Meme
is paid to the governed fee-policy destination. A migrated sale's exact `PresaleCap` holder may
schedule a replacement through `presale_vault::schedule_fee_split`, supplying the proposed
`FeeSplit`, next notice in milliseconds and `Clock`. The initial notice is 48 hours
(`172_800_000` milliseconds). The full applied notice governs every change, including a reduction
to zero; replacing a proposal restarts that wait. Both value and notice stay applied until explicit
activation. A delay-only change is valid; unchanged value and notice abort with code 20
(`EUnchanged`) from Blast admin's `delayed` module.

The same cap holder may call `presale_vault::cancel_fee_split` even when the proposal is ready.
Cancellation retains applied policy. At or after readiness, anyone may call
`blast_presale::bluefin::settle_and_apply_fee_split` or
`blast_presale::cetus::settle_and_apply_fee_split`, supplying the usual fee-collection objects and
`Clock`. These collect all position fees under the old split before activating the stored split
and notice, and accept no caller-selected replacement. Fees already allocated to holders stay
