### `blast_admin::delayed`

Settings that change only after their applied notice, and the deadline rules every delayed type shares.  A timelock in the Compound/OpenZeppelin sense: schedule, wait the applied notice, then apply; cancellable until applied. Settings live here; one-shot actions in `delayed_action`, allowlists in `delayed_set` and keyed values in `delayed_map`.  Every value carries an owner-defined key `K` and the ID of the object that stores it. Constructors take that object's `&UID`, which only the code creating or holding the object has, so no package can attribute a value or its events to another's object. Owners use a struct without a public constructor as `K`, so only their module can pack it. Each delayed module emits every lifecycle fact of its type, generic in `K` and carrying `owner`; owners emit only their own side effects.  Every change, a shorter notice included, waits the notice applied when it was scheduled. A notice can start at zero, so a schedule and its apply in one transaction then act as a setter; there is no other mutation path. No notice exceeds `max_delay_ms`, so a notice can always be changed again. Readers need no Clock.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/admin/sources/delayed/delayed.move

#### Types

```move
/// An applied setting, its applied notice and at most one proposed replacement.
public struct Delayed<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store> has store {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    value: T,
    delay_ms: u64,
    pending: Option<Proposal<T>>,
}

/// A proposed value and the notice in force once it applies, ready from `ready_at_ms`.
public struct Proposal<T: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop, store {
    value: T,
    delay_ms: u64,
    ready_at_ms: u64,
}

/// A notice period and the time it elapses: the notice an admission or entry change waits,
/// or a proposed next notice. Either is ready from `ready_at_ms`.
public struct Notice has copy, drop, store {
    delay_ms: u64,
    ready_at_ms: u64,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// A setting in force at once; every later change waits the applied notice.
public fun new<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store>(
    key: K,
    owner: &UID,
    value: T,
    delay_ms: u64,
): Delayed<K, T>

/// The longest notice any delayed type accepts, in milliseconds.
public fun max_delay_ms(): u64

/// The applied value.
public fun value<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store>(self: &Delayed<K, T>): T

/// The applied notice in milliseconds.
public fun delay_ms<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store>(self: &Delayed<K, T>): u64

/// True when every change still to come waits a nonzero notice: the applied notice is nonzero
/// and no proposal would set it to zero.
public fun is_guarded<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store>(self: &Delayed<K, T>): bool

/// The proposed replacement, if any.
public fun pending<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &Delayed<K, T>,
): Option<Proposal<T>>

/// Proposes `value` and the next notice `delay_ms`, ready after the applied notice, and
/// returns when. A replaced proposal is cancelled and the full applied notice restarts.
/// Aborts when the proposal would change neither the value nor the notice.
public fun schedule<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut Delayed<K, T>,
    value: T,
    delay_ms: u64,
    clock: &Clock,
): u64

/// Proposes only a new value, keeping the applied notice.
public fun schedule_value<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut Delayed<K, T>,
    value: T,
    clock: &Clock,
): u64

/// Proposes only a new notice, keeping the applied value. A shorter notice, zero included,
/// still waits the applied one.
public fun schedule_delay<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut Delayed<K, T>,
    delay_ms: u64,
    clock: &Clock,
): u64

/// Checks that `apply` would succeed now, changing nothing. Owners call it before
/// settling accrued economics under the applied value in the same transaction.
public fun assert_ready<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &Delayed<K, T>,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Applies the ready proposal's value and notice together and returns the new value.
public fun apply<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut Delayed<K, T>,
    clock: &Clock,
): T

/// Discards the proposal, even a ready one, leaving the applied value and notice.
public fun cancel<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store>(self: &mut Delayed<K, T>)

/// Deletes a setting with no proposal and records its end; cancel a proposal first.
public fun destroy<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store>(self: Delayed<K, T>)

/// The proposed value, or the proposed change for an action slot.
public fun proposal_value<T: copy + drop + store>(self: &Proposal<T>): T

/// The notice in force once the proposal applies.
public fun proposal_delay_ms<T: copy + drop + store>(self: &Proposal<T>): u64

/// The Unix millisecond time from which the proposal can apply.
public fun ready_at_ms<T: copy + drop + store>(self: &Proposal<T>): u64

/// The notice waited, or the proposed next notice.
public fun notice_delay_ms(self: &Notice): u64

/// The Unix millisecond time from which the change can apply.
public fun notice_ready_at_ms(self: &Notice): u64
```

#### Events

```move
/// A setting was created with its first applied value and notice.
public struct DelayedCreated<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    value: T,
    delay_ms: u64,
}

/// A replacement value and next notice were proposed, ready from `ready_at_ms`.
public struct DelayedScheduled<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    value: T,
    delay_ms: u64,
    ready_at_ms: u64,
}

/// A proposal was discarded, by cancellation or by a replacing schedule.
public struct DelayedCancelled<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    value: T,
    delay_ms: u64,
    ready_at_ms: u64,
}

/// A ready proposal became the applied value and notice.
public struct DelayedApplied<K: copy + drop + store, T: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    previous_value: T,
    value: T,
    delay_ms: u64,
}

/// A setting was deleted with nothing pending.
public struct DelayedDestroyed<K: copy + drop + store, phantom T: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
}
```

#### Constants

- `MAX_DELAY_MS: u64 = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000`: The longest notice any delayed value, action, set or map accepts: 30 days.

### `blast_admin::delayed_action`

One-shot actions, such as an upgrade or a capability reassignment, that run only after their slot's applied notice. The slot also governs its own notice. See `delayed` for the rules every delayed type shares.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/admin/sources/delayed/delayed_action.move

#### Types

```move
/// An applied notice and at most one proposed one-shot action or notice change.
public struct DelayedAction<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store> has store {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    delay_ms: u64,
    pending: Option<delayed::Proposal<Change<A>>>,
}

/// What a proposal does once applied.
public enum Change<A: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop, store {
    /// Hands the owner its action; the notice stays as applied.
    Action(A),
    /// Changes only the notice, to the proposal's `delay_ms`.
    Delay,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// An action slot with nothing proposed; every action waits the applied notice.
public fun new<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store>(
    key: K,
    owner: &UID,
    delay_ms: u64,
): DelayedAction<K, A>

/// The applied notice in milliseconds.
public fun delay_ms<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store>(self: &DelayedAction<K, A>): u64

/// True when every action still to come waits a nonzero notice: the applied notice is nonzero
/// and no proposal would set it to zero.
public fun is_guarded<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &DelayedAction<K, A>,
): bool

/// The proposed action or notice change, if any.
public fun pending<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &DelayedAction<K, A>,
): Option<delayed::Proposal<Change<A>>>

/// Proposes `action`, ready after the applied notice, and returns when. A replaced
/// proposal is cancelled and the full applied notice restarts.
public fun schedule<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedAction<K, A>,
    action: A,
    clock: &Clock,
): u64

/// Proposes only a new notice, ready after the applied one, replacing any proposed action.
public fun schedule_delay<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedAction<K, A>,
    delay_ms: u64,
    clock: &Clock,
): u64

/// Consumes the ready proposed action and returns it for the owner to perform.
/// Aborts when the proposal is a notice change.
public fun take_action<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedAction<K, A>,
    clock: &Clock,
): A

/// Applies the ready proposed notice. Aborts when the proposal is an action.
public fun apply_delay<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedAction<K, A>,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Discards the proposal, even a ready one, leaving the applied notice.
public fun cancel<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store>(self: &mut DelayedAction<K, A>)

/// Deletes an action slot with no proposal and records its end; cancel a proposal first.
public fun destroy<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store>(self: DelayedAction<K, A>)

/// The proposed action, or none for a notice change.
public fun action<A: copy + drop + store>(self: &Change<A>): Option<A>
```

#### Events

```move
/// An action slot was created with its first applied notice.
public struct ActionCreated<K: copy + drop + store, phantom A: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    delay_ms: u64,
}

/// An action or notice change was proposed, ready from `ready_at_ms`; `delay_ms` is the
/// notice in force once it applies.
public struct ActionScheduled<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    change: Change<A>,
    delay_ms: u64,
    ready_at_ms: u64,
}

/// A proposed action or notice change was discarded, by cancellation or replacement.
public struct ActionCancelled<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    change: Change<A>,
    delay_ms: u64,
    ready_at_ms: u64,
}

/// A ready action was handed to its owner, or a notice change applied.
public struct ActionApplied<K: copy + drop + store, A: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    change: Change<A>,
    delay_ms: u64,
}

/// An action slot was deleted with nothing pending.
public struct ActionDestroyed<K: copy + drop + store, phantom A: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
}
```

### `blast_admin::delayed_map`

Keyed values under one shared notice, such as per-coin overrides. Every entry change, setting or clearing, waits the notice applied when it was scheduled, and its deadline is fixed then; a later notice change never moves it. See `delayed` for the shared rules.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/admin/sources/delayed/delayed_map.move

#### Types

```move
/// Applied values by entry, one applied notice, at most one pending change per entry, and at
/// most one proposed notice. Values live in a Table, so reads cost one entry and the map
/// grows without bound; pending changes are few and live inline.
public struct DelayedMap<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store> has store {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    entries: Table<E, V>,
    delay_ms: u64,
    pending: VecMap<E, EntryProposal<V>>,
    pending_delay: Option<delayed::Notice>,
}

/// A proposed entry value, or none to clear the entry, and the notice it waits.
public struct EntryProposal<V: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop, store {
    value: Option<V>,
    notice: delayed::Notice,
}

/// What a map proposal does once applied.
public enum MapChange<E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop, store {
    /// Sets the entry to `value`, or clears it when `value` is none.
    Entry {
        entry: E,
        value: Option<V>,
    },
    /// Changes the notice for later entry changes.
    Delay,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// An empty map; every entry change waits the applied notice.
public fun new<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store>(
    key: K,
    owner: &UID,
    delay_ms: u64,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
): DelayedMap<K, E, V>

/// The applied value of `entry`, or none when it has none.
public fun value<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &DelayedMap<K, E, V>,
    entry: &E,
): Option<V>

/// The applied notice for entry changes, in milliseconds.
public fun delay_ms<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &DelayedMap<K, E, V>,
): u64

/// The pending change of `entry`, if any.
public fun pending<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &DelayedMap<K, E, V>,
    entry: &E,
): Option<EntryProposal<V>>

/// The proposed next notice, if any.
public fun pending_delay<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &DelayedMap<K, E, V>,
): Option<delayed::Notice>

/// Proposes setting `entry` to `value` (none clears it) after the applied notice, and
/// returns when. A replaced change is cancelled and the full notice restarts. Aborts when
/// `value` is already the applied value.
public fun schedule<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedMap<K, E, V>,
    entry: E,
    value: Option<V>,
    clock: &Clock,
): u64

/// Applies `entry`'s ready change: sets its value or clears it.
public fun apply<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedMap<K, E, V>,
    entry: E,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Discards `entry`'s pending change, even a ready one.
public fun cancel<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedMap<K, E, V>,
    entry: E,
)

/// Proposes only a new notice, ready after the applied one, and returns when. Pending
/// entry changes keep their deadlines.
public fun schedule_delay<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedMap<K, E, V>,
    delay_ms: u64,
    clock: &Clock,
): u64

/// Applies the ready proposed notice to later entry changes.
public fun apply_delay<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedMap<K, E, V>,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Discards the proposed notice, even a ready one.
public fun cancel_delay<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedMap<K, E, V>,
)

/// Deletes a map with no pending entry or notice change and records its end, which also
/// ends every remaining entry.
public fun destroy<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store>(
    self: DelayedMap<K, E, V>,
)

/// The proposed value, or none when the change clears the entry.
public fun entry_proposal_value<V: copy + drop + store>(self: &EntryProposal<V>): Option<V>

/// The notice the change waits and when it becomes ready.
public fun entry_proposal_notice<V: copy + drop + store>(self: &EntryProposal<V>): delayed::Notice
```

#### Events

```move
/// A map was created empty with its first applied notice.
public struct MapCreated<K: copy + drop + store, phantom E: copy + drop + store, phantom V: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    delay_ms: u64,
}

/// An entry change or notice change was proposed, ready from `ready_at_ms`. `delay_ms` is
/// the notice an entry change waits, or the proposed next notice.
public struct MapScheduled<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    change: MapChange<E, V>,
    delay_ms: u64,
    ready_at_ms: u64,
}

/// A proposed change was discarded, by cancellation or replacement; its fields match its
/// `MapScheduled`.
public struct MapCancelled<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    change: MapChange<E, V>,
    delay_ms: u64,
    ready_at_ms: u64,
}

/// An entry was set or cleared, or a notice change applied; `delay_ms` matches its
/// `MapScheduled`.
public struct MapApplied<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store, V: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    change: MapChange<E, V>,
    delay_ms: u64,
}

/// A map was deleted with nothing pending, ending every remaining entry.
public struct MapDestroyed<K: copy + drop + store, phantom E: copy + drop + store, phantom V: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
}
```

### `blast_admin::delayed_set`

Allowlists whose members join only after the applied notice and leave at once. See `delayed` for the rules every delayed type shares.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/admin/sources/delayed/delayed_set.move

#### Types

```move
/// Admitted members, one applied notice for new admissions, pending admissions with fixed
/// deadlines, and at most one proposed notice. A notice change never moves a deadline.
public struct DelayedSet<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store> has store {
    owner: ID,
    key: K,
    members: VecSet<E>,
    delay_ms: u64,
    admissions: VecMap<E, delayed::Notice>,
    pending_delay: Option<delayed::Notice>,
}

/// What a set proposal does once applied.
public enum SetChange<E: copy + drop + store> has copy, drop, store {
    /// Admits the member.
    Admission(E),
    /// Changes the notice for later admissions.
    Delay,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// An empty set; every admission waits the applied notice.
public fun new<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(
    key: K,
    owner: &UID,
    delay_ms: u64,
): DelayedSet<K, E>

/// Whether `member` has been admitted and not removed.
public fun contains<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &DelayedSet<K, E>,
    member: &E,
): bool

/// The admitted members.
public fun members<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &DelayedSet<K, E>,
): VecSet<E>

/// The applied notice for new admissions, in milliseconds.
public fun delay_ms<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(self: &DelayedSet<K, E>): u64

/// When `member`'s pending admission becomes ready, if one is pending.
public fun admission_ready_at_ms<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &DelayedSet<K, E>,
    member: &E,
): Option<u64>

/// How many admissions are pending.
public fun pending_count<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &DelayedSet<K, E>,
): u64

/// True when every admission still to come waits a nonzero notice: the applied notice is
/// nonzero, no proposal would set it to zero, and no admission scheduled earlier is pending.
public fun is_guarded<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(self: &DelayedSet<K, E>): bool

/// The proposed next notice, if any.
public fun pending_delay<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &DelayedSet<K, E>,
): Option<delayed::Notice>

/// Proposes admitting `member` after the applied notice (never a proposed one) and returns
/// when. Rescheduling a pending member cancels its admission and restarts the notice.
/// Aborts when `member` is already admitted.
public fun schedule_add<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedSet<K, E>,
    member: E,
    clock: &Clock,
): u64

/// Admits `member` once its admission is ready.
public fun apply_add<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedSet<K, E>,
    member: E,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Discards `member`'s pending admission, even a ready one.
public fun cancel_add<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedSet<K, E>,
    member: E,
)

/// Removes `member` at once and discards its pending admission, leaving the notice.
/// Aborts when `member` is neither admitted nor pending.
public fun remove<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedSet<K, E>,
    member: E,
)

/// Proposes only a new notice, ready after the applied one, and returns when. Pending
/// admissions keep their deadlines.
public fun schedule_delay<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedSet<K, E>,
    delay_ms: u64,
    clock: &Clock,
): u64

/// Applies the ready proposed notice to later admissions.
public fun apply_delay<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(
    self: &mut DelayedSet<K, E>,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Discards the proposed notice, even a ready one.
public fun cancel_delay<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(self: &mut DelayedSet<K, E>)

/// Deletes a set with no pending admission or notice change and records its end, which
/// also ends every remaining membership.
public fun destroy<K: copy + drop + store, E: copy + drop + store>(self: DelayedSet<K, E>)
```

### `blast_admin::operational_version`

Sealed operational-generation arithmetic for consumer-owned version containers.

#### Types

/// Storable, package-typed generation value with construction and mutation sealed here.
public struct OperationalVersion<phantom PackageMarker: drop> has store {
    generation: u64,
}
```

#### Functions

/// Creates the initial operational generation from the consumer package's one-time witness, so
/// the value can only come into existence inside that package's initializer.
public fun new<PackageMarker: drop>(otw: &PackageMarker): OperationalVersion<PackageMarker>

/// Rejects bytecode whose private compiled generation differs from canonical state.
public fun assert_current<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &OperationalVersion<PackageMarker>,
    compiled_generation: u64,
)

/// Proves the proposed compiled generation is exactly next before other finalizer effects.
public fun assert_next<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &OperationalVersion<PackageMarker>,
    compiled_generation: u64,
)

///
/// `container` is the versioned object's own UID, so the emitted container ID is one the caller
/// holds.
public fun advance<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut OperationalVersion<PackageMarker>,
    container: &UID,
    compiled_generation: u64,
)
```

#### Constants

- `INITIAL_GENERATION: u64 = 1`

### `blast_admin::package_admin`

One package's sealed Publisher and UpgradeCap, its delayed upgrade decisions, and the role-gated pause controls of its `PackageVersion`, typed by the package's one-time witness.  Each role is generic over the package marker, so the ACL stores `UpgradeAdmin<A>` and `UpgradeAdmin<B>` as distinct grants and one package's administrator never reaches another's custody. This package is immutable: no consumer bytecode generation gates these calls, and a consumer whose new bytecode compiles the wrong generation can still schedule a repair.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/admin/sources/package_admin.move

#### Types

```move
/// The exact code digest or irreversible end of upgrades approved for execution.
public enum UpgradeAction has copy, drop, store {
    Upgrade(vector<u8>),
    MakeImmutable,
}

/// Keys the delayed lifecycle of one package's upgrade actions and their notice.
public struct UpgradeKey<phantom PackageMarker: drop>() has copy, drop, store;

/// Shared custody for one package's framework Publisher and UpgradeCap.
public struct PackageAdmin<phantom PackageMarker: drop> has key {
    id: UID,
    custody: upgrade_custody::UpgradeCustody<PackageMarker>,
    upgrade: delayed_action::DelayedAction<UpgradeKey<PackageMarker>, UpgradeAction>,
}

/// Schedules and executes the package's upgrades and immutability, and changes their notice.
public struct UpgradeAdmin<phantom PackageMarker> {}

/// May set the package's pause bits immediately, never clear them.
public struct PauseAdmin<phantom PackageMarker> {}

/// May clear the package's pause bits, only through the package's own unpause.
public struct UnpauseAdmin<phantom PackageMarker> {}

/// May cancel the package's scheduled upgrade action or notice change.
public struct CancelAdmin<phantom PackageMarker> {}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// Consumes the unique publication proof, seals the native capabilities and shares both the
/// administration and the package version. The version starts with every defined bit paused;
/// an `UnpauseAdmin` releases it through the package's own unpause.
public fun wrap<PackageMarker: drop>(
    publication: package_version::Publication<PackageMarker>,
    upgrade_cap: UpgradeCap,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
)

/// Schedules one exact code digest under the applied notice, replacing any previous action.
/// Changing the notice requires a separate notice-only proposal. Aborts once the package is
/// immutable.
public fun schedule_upgrade<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut PackageAdmin<PackageMarker>,
    _: &blast_acl::AdminWitness<UpgradeAdmin<PackageMarker>>,
    digest: vector<u8>,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Schedules the irreversible destruction of upgrade authority under the applied notice.
/// Aborts once the package is immutable.
public fun schedule_make_immutable<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut PackageAdmin<PackageMarker>,
    _: &blast_acl::AdminWitness<UpgradeAdmin<PackageMarker>>,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Cancels the scheduled action or notice change, even after its execution threshold.
public fun cancel_upgrade_action<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut PackageAdmin<PackageMarker>,
    _: &blast_acl::AdminWitness<CancelAdmin<PackageMarker>>,
)

/// Consumes the ready upgrade action for exactly `digest` and authorizes it under the sealed
/// cap's current policy.
public fun authorize_upgrade<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut PackageAdmin<PackageMarker>,
    _: &blast_acl::AdminWitness<UpgradeAdmin<PackageMarker>>,
    digest: vector<u8>,
    clock: &Clock,
): UpgradeTicket

/// Commits the native receipt into the sealed cap and advances the package version by one
/// generation, together. The new bytecode must compile that generation; bytecode compiling any
/// other fails every `assert_current`, while these calls stay available to schedule a repair.
public fun commit_upgrade_and_advance<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut PackageAdmin<PackageMarker>,
    _: &blast_acl::AdminWitness<UpgradeAdmin<PackageMarker>>,
    package_version: &mut package_version::PackageVersion<PackageMarker>,
    receipt: UpgradeReceipt,
)

/// Consumes the ready immutability action and irreversibly destroys native upgrade authority.
public fun make_immutable<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut PackageAdmin<PackageMarker>,
    _: &blast_acl::AdminWitness<UpgradeAdmin<PackageMarker>>,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Proposes only a new upgrade notice, ready after the applied one; replaces any pending
/// upgrade or immutability action.
public fun schedule_upgrade_delay<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut PackageAdmin<PackageMarker>,
    _: &blast_acl::AdminWitness<UpgradeAdmin<PackageMarker>>,
    delay_ms: u64,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Applies a ready notice-only proposal; anyone may call it, and it cannot consume an action.
public fun apply_upgrade_delay<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut PackageAdmin<PackageMarker>,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Sets the requested pause bits immediately.
public fun pause<PackageMarker: drop>(
    package_version: &mut package_version::PackageVersion<PackageMarker>,
    _: &blast_acl::AdminWitness<PauseAdmin<PackageMarker>>,
    bits: u8,
)

/// Clears the requested pause bits for the package's own unpause, which first checks its own
/// configuration notices and then passes a value of the exact witness type the package pinned
/// at publication. Aborts while any upgrade notice still to come could be zero. Only the
/// package's unpause constructs that type, so a role alone cannot skip its checks.
public fun clear_pause_bits<PackageMarker: drop, UnpauseWitness: drop>(
    self: &PackageAdmin<PackageMarker>,
    _: &blast_acl::AdminWitness<UnpauseAdmin<PackageMarker>>,
    _: UnpauseWitness,
    package_version: &mut package_version::PackageVersion<PackageMarker>,
    bits: u8,
)
```

#### Constants

- `INITIAL_UPGRADE_DELAY_MS: u64 = 48 * 60 * 60 * 1_000`: The notice every upgrade or immutability action waits from publication until changed.

### `blast_admin::package_version`

One package's publication proof, operational generation and pause bits, typed by its one-time witness.  The consumer's initializer turns its one-time witness into an owned `Publication`, which `package_admin::wrap` later converts into the shared `PackageVersion`, fully paused. The consumer compiles its own generation constant and checks it with `assert_current`; it also chooses which pause bits exist and pins the one witness type its own unpause passes when clearing them. Setting and clearing bits and advancing the generation are sealed here and reached only through `package_admin`'s role-gated calls.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/admin/sources/package_version.move

#### Types

```move
/// Owned publication custody; it cannot supply the `PackageVersion` that operations require.
public struct Publication<phantom PackageMarker: drop> has key {
    id: UID,
    publisher: Publisher,
    valid_pause_bits: u8,
    unpause_witness: TypeName,
    generation: operational_version::OperationalVersion<PackageMarker>,
}

/// The package's shared operational generation and pause bits.
public struct PackageVersion<phantom PackageMarker: drop> has key {
    id: UID,
    /// The bits this package defines; every pause or unpause request must fall within them.
    valid_pause_bits: u8,
    paused: u8,
    /// The exact type, with defining IDs, whose value the package's own unpause passes to
    /// `package_admin::clear_pause_bits`.
    unpause_witness: TypeName,
    generation: operational_version::OperationalVersion<PackageMarker>,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// Claims the Publisher and seeds the first generation from the package's one-time witness,
/// so a publication can only come into existence inside that package's initializer.
/// `valid_pause_bits` fixes the bits the package defines, and zero defines none.
/// `UnpauseWitness` pins the one type that can clear them: a struct the package defines, other
/// than its marker, that it constructs only inside its own unpause and never returns or stores.
public fun new_publication<PackageMarker: drop, UnpauseWitness: drop>(
    otw: PackageMarker,
    valid_pause_bits: u8,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
): Publication<PackageMarker>

/// Transfers the publication to the transaction sender, who later wraps it with the
/// package's `UpgradeCap`.
public fun keep<PackageMarker: drop>(self: Publication<PackageMarker>, ctx: &mut TxContext)

/// Rejects callable bytecode whose compiled generation is not the active one.
public fun assert_current<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &PackageVersion<PackageMarker>,
    compiled_generation: u64,
)

/// Rejects an operation whose pause bit is set, before its lifecycle or economic checks. This is a
/// mask check only: a bit the package never defined is never set, so it never aborts.
public fun assert_not_paused<PackageMarker: drop>(self: &PackageVersion<PackageMarker>, bit: u8)
```

### `blast_admin::upgrade_custody`

Sealed custody and native transitions for one consumer package's framework capabilities.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/admin/sources/upgrade_custody.move

#### Types

```move
/// Storable custody value whose capabilities never leave it: the Publisher is readable by
/// reference and the UpgradeCap acts only through the named transitions below.
public struct UpgradeCustody<phantom PackageMarker: drop> has store {
    publisher: Publisher,
    upgrade_cap: Option<UpgradeCap>,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// Validates an original package's Publisher and never-upgraded cap before sealing both.
public fun new<PackageMarker: drop>(
    custodian_id: ID,
    publisher: Publisher,
    upgrade_cap: UpgradeCap,
): UpgradeCustody<PackageMarker>

/// Reports whether native upgrade authority remains sealed in custody.
public fun has_upgrade_cap<PackageMarker: drop>(self: &UpgradeCustody<PackageMarker>): bool

/// Borrows the sealed Publisher for provenance-gated framework features such as Display and
/// TransferPolicy. Every framework path that moves or burns a Publisher takes it by value, so a
/// reference cannot end custody; the consumer wrapper decides who may call this.
public fun publisher<PackageMarker: drop>(self: &UpgradeCustody<PackageMarker>): &Publisher

/// Authorizes exactly one 32-byte package digest under the cap's current policy.
public fun authorize_upgrade<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut UpgradeCustody<PackageMarker>,
    custodian_id: ID,
    digest: vector<u8>,
): UpgradeTicket

/// Commits a native receipt into the same sealed capability that authorized it.
public fun commit_upgrade<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut UpgradeCustody<PackageMarker>,
    custodian_id: ID,
    receipt: UpgradeReceipt,
)

/// Irreversibly narrows compatible policy to additive-only upgrades.
public fun restrict_to_additive<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut UpgradeCustody<PackageMarker>,
    custodian_id: ID,
)

/// Irreversibly narrows compatible or additive policy to dependency-only upgrades.
public fun restrict_to_dependency_only<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut UpgradeCustody<PackageMarker>,
    custodian_id: ID,
)

/// Irreversibly destroys native upgrade authority while preserving Publisher custody.
public fun make_immutable<PackageMarker: drop>(
    self: &mut UpgradeCustody<PackageMarker>,
    custodian_id: ID,
)
```

#### Constants

- `PACKAGE_DIGEST_LENGTH: u64 = 32`
- `INITIAL_NATIVE_VERSION: u64 = 1`: The framework stamps a freshly published package's `UpgradeCap` with version one.

## API reference: `blast_aftermath_dao_presale` (Aftermath DAO-pool presale migrator)

Live on mainnet, published from an earlier revision. The source documented here has changed since; until it is republished, confirm signatures against the live package.

Events: payload structs are emitted directly, each under its own type.

### `blast_aftermath_dao_presale::blast_aftermath_dao_presale`

A one-off `blast_presale` migrator built for a partner. The `AdminCap` creates each sale with the Aftermath pool-creation capability of its LP coin, which stays bound to that sale. Anyone may then migrate the funded sale into a 50/50 Aftermath weighted pool wrapped in Aftermath's DAO-fee pool, which pays a 2% fee on every swap, deposit, and withdrawal straight to the partner treasury. The treasury also receives each sale's `PresaleCap` and each DAO-fee pool's owner cap, with which it may change that pool's fee or recipient; the sale's LP is locked forever.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/vendors/aftermath_dao_presale/sources/blast_aftermath_dao_presale.move

#### Types

```move
/// Sealed migrator identity a sale fixes when `new` starts it. Only this module constructs it, so
/// only `migrate` can release that sale's liquidity.
public struct Witness() has drop;

/// The package's only administrator, sent to the publisher at publication. Its one power is
/// creating sales through `new` and `finalize`.
public struct AdminCap has key, store {
    id: UID,
}

/// Shared reservation of one sale's Aftermath pool creation: the `CreatePoolCapV2` of the fresh LP
/// coin `Lp`, which only `migrate` of the sale `presale_id` can consume. A sale `new` started but
/// finalized directly in `blast_presale` has none, so it can never migrate and refunds after its
/// LP deadline.
public struct PoolCreation<phantom Lp> has key {
    id: UID,
    presale_id: ID,
    create_pool_cap: pool::CreatePoolCapV2,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// Starts a presale that migrates through this module. Its pool's weights and fees are this
/// module's constants, so the sale carries no pool terms. The sale is set like any other, then
/// finalized only through this module's `finalize`, which reserves its pool creation. The
/// `CreationPolicy` must allow `Witness`.
public fun new<SaleToken, Quote>(
    _: &AdminCap,
    package_version: &blast_presale::blast_presale_package::PackageVersion,
    treasury_cap: TreasuryCap<SaleToken>,
    creation_policy: &blast_presale::creation_policy::CreationPolicy,
    fee_policy: &blast_presale::fee_policy::FeePolicy,
): blast_presale::blast_presale::PresaleInitializer<SaleToken, Quote>

/// Finalizes a sale `new` started, sends its `PresaleCap` to the treasury, and shares a
/// `PoolCreation` binding `create_pool_cap`, minted by the fresh LP coin `Lp`, to it. Every LP fee
/// its pool pays reaches the treasury, so this sets the sale's LP-fee split to name the treasury as
/// its only recipient. The initializer must be one `new` started: another migrator's sale could
/// never consume the pool creation.
public fun finalize<Lp, SaleToken, Quote>(
    _: &AdminCap,
    package_version: &blast_presale::blast_presale_package::PackageVersion,
    initializer: blast_presale::blast_presale::PresaleInitializer<SaleToken, Quote>,
    currency: &mut Currency<SaleToken>,
    create_pool_cap: pool::CreatePoolCapV2,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
): blast_presale::blast_presale::Presale<SaleToken, Quote>

/// Anyone may migrate a funded sale `finalize` created, consuming the `PoolCreation` bound to it: it
/// seeds a 50/50 Aftermath pool with all of the sale's LP tokens and Quote, wraps it in a DAO-fee
/// pool paying the treasury, shares that pool, sends its owner cap to the treasury, and locks the
/// LP at `BURN_ADDRESS`.
public fun migrate<Lp, SaleToken, Quote>(
    sale: &mut blast_presale::blast_presale::Presale<SaleToken, Quote>,
    package_version: &blast_presale::blast_presale_package::PackageVersion,
    pool_creation: PoolCreation<Lp>,
    fee_policy: &blast_presale::fee_policy::FeePolicy,
    pool_registry: &mut pool_registry::PoolRegistry,
    dao_fee_version: &version::Version,
    clock: &Clock,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
)
```

#### Events

```move
/// `finalize` reserved the sale `presale_id`'s Aftermath pool creation for the LP coin `Lp` in the
/// shared `pool_creation_id`, which its migration consumes.
public struct PoolCreationReserved<phantom Lp, phantom SaleToken, phantom Quote> has copy, drop {
    presale_id: ID,
    pool_creation_id: ID,
}

/// A sale migrated into the Aftermath pool `pool_id`, which traders reach through the shared
/// DAO-fee pool `dao_fee_pool_id`. The treasury holds that pool's owner cap `owner_cap_id`, and
/// `BURN_ADDRESS` holds the LP coin `lp_coin_id`, which locks the sale's `lp` units forever.
public struct Migrated<phantom Lp, phantom SaleToken, phantom Quote> has copy, drop {
    presale_id: ID,
    pool_id: ID,
    dao_fee_pool_id: ID,
    owner_cap_id: ID,
    lp_coin_id: ID,
    lp: u64,
}
```

#### Errors

| Constant | Code | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EPoolMismatch` | 0 | The Aftermath pool must hold every sale token and Quote unit the presale released. |
| `EDaoFeePoolMismatch` | 1 | The DAO-fee pool must charge this package's fee and pay the treasury. |
| `EWrongPresale` | 2 | The pool creation is bound to a different presale. |
| `EWrongMigrator` | 3 | Only a sale this package's `new` started can be finalized here. |

#### Constants

- `TREASURY: address = @0x37cf46b499f740e653644bd2f7a8ed97f248e8b3c69d5d12c97d7845a54c0cd8`: Receives every sale's `PresaleCap` and every pool's DAO fees and owner cap.
- `BURN_ADDRESS: address = @0x0`: Owns every pool's LP coin. No one can sign for the zero address, so nothing it owns can ever be used in a transaction again.
- `DAO_FEE_BPS: u16 = 200`: The DAO fee, 2%, that Aftermath sends to the treasury from every swap, deposit, and withdrawal until the owner cap changes it.
- `HALF_WEIGHT: u64 = 500_000_000_000_000_000`: Each coin's weight: half of Aftermath's `1e18` fixed-point one.
- `FLATNESS: u64 = 0`: Selects Aftermath's uncorrelated weighted-product curve.
- `BASE_SWAP_FEE: u64 = 100_000_000_000_000`: Aftermath's minimum base swap-in fee, 0.01% in its `1e18` unit; it rejects zero. This part compounds into the locked LP.
- `POOL_NAME: vector<u8> = b"Blast Presale Pool"`
- `ALL_BPS: u64 = 10_000`: The whole LP-fee split, which the treasury takes.
